## Page 3950

He—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked about someone who believes that good comes from Allah and evil comes from Satan, and that evil lies in the servant’s hands: if he wishes, he does it, and if he wishes, he refrains. When challenged about this, he says:

Allah Most High says:
“Indeed, Allah does not command indecency.”

“Indeed, Allah has no need of you, and He does not approve of disbelief for His servants.”

This person believes that good comes from Allah and that evil lies in his own hands, so that whenever he wants to do evil, he does it. He says: “I have a will, and whenever I want to do evil, I do it.” Does he have an effective will or not?

He replied:

All praise is due to Allah.

This matter rests upon two premises.

The first is that the servant should know that Allah commands faith and righteous deeds; that He loves and approves of good deeds, honours those who perform them, rewards them, takes them as His allies, and is pleased with them. He loves them, and they love Him. They are Allah’s army, granted victory, and Allah’s party, who prevail. They are His God-fearing allies, His successful party, and His righteous servants, the people of Paradise. They are the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. They are those who follow the straight path—the path of those whom You have blessed, not those who have incurred Your anger or those who have gone astray.

The servant should also know that Allah has forbidden evil deeds—disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience—and that He hates these things and detests those who commit them. He curses them, is angry with them, punishes them, and is their enemy. They are the enemies of Allah and His Messenger, the allies of Satan, and the people of the Fire

---

## Page 3951

and they are the wretched. Yet they are close to one another in this respect, ranging from a disbeliever to a wicked person to a sinner who is neither a disbeliever nor a wicked person.

The second premise is that the servant should know that Allah is the Lord, Creator, and Sovereign of everything. There is no Lord besides Him and no Creator other than Him. Whatever He wills comes to pass, and whatever He does not will does not come to pass. There is no might or power except through Him, and no refuge from Him except with Him. He has power over all things.

Everything in the heavens and the earth—all entities, their attributes, and their movements—is created by Him, subject to His power, and directed according to His will. Nothing lies beyond His power and dominion, and no one shares any of this with Him. Rather, He—glorified is He—is the only God; He alone has no partner. His is the dominion, and His is all praise, and He has power over all things. The servant is utterly dependent upon Allah in everything, needing Him in every matter and unable to do without Him even for the blink of an eye. Whoever Allah guides, none can lead astray; and whoever He leads astray, none can guide.

Once these two “premises” are established, we say:

If the servant is inspired to ask Allah for guidance and seek His help in obeying Him, Allah helps and guides him, and this becomes a means of his happiness in this world and the Hereafter. But if the servant is forsaken, so that he neither worships Allah, seeks His help, nor places his trust in Him, he is left to his own might and power. Allah then makes Satan his ally, and he is turned away from the path and becomes wretched in this world and the Hereafter.

Everything that occurs in existence is by Allah’s decree and predestination. No one escapes the destiny decreed for him or goes beyond what has been written for him in the Preserved Tablet, and against Allah no one has

---

## Page 3952

any argument. Rather,

“To Allah belongs the conclusive argument. Had He willed, He would have guided you all.”

Every blessing from Him is a grace, and every affliction from Him is just. The servant must believe in predestination, but he may not invoke it as an argument against Allah. Belief in it is guidance, whereas invoking it as an argument against Allah is misguidance and error. Rather, belief in predestination requires the servant to be steadfastly patient and deeply grateful: patient in adversity and grateful in prosperity. When he receives a blessing, he knows that it is from Allah and thanks Him, whether that blessing is a good deed he has performed or some benefit attained through his efforts. It is Allah who facilitates the performance of good deeds, and He who graciously rewards them. To Him, therefore, belongs all praise for all of this.

When a calamity befalls him, he bears it patiently, even if it has come at another person’s hands. It is Allah who gave that person power over him and created that person’s actions, and the calamity had been decreed for the servant. As the Most High says:

“No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves except that it is recorded in a Book before We bring it into being. That is surely easy for Allah.”

“So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you, nor exult over what He has given you.”

And the Most High says:

“No calamity befalls except by Allah’s permission. And whoever believes in Allah, He will guide his heart.”

They said: “This is the man whom a calamity befalls, who knows that it is from Allah and so accepts it and submits.”

When the servant sins, he must seek forgiveness and repent, rather than invoke predestination as an argument against Allah. He must not say, “What blame is mine when this sin was predestined for me?” Rather, he must know that he himself is the sinner, the disobedient one who committed the sin, even though all of this occurs by Allah’s decree, predestination, and will. For nothing comes to pass except through His will, power, and creation. Yet it is the servant who consumed what was unlawful and committed the indecent act,

---

## Page 3953

and it is he who wronged himself; just as it is he who prayed, fasted, performed Hajj, and strove in Allah’s cause. These actions are attributed to him: he is the one who makes these movements and acquires these acts brought into being. To his credit is what he has earned, and against him is what he has incurred. Allah is the Creator of all this and everything else, in accordance with His consummate wisdom, through His perfect power and His irresistible will.

The Most High says:

“So be patient. Indeed, Allah’s promise is true, and seek forgiveness for your sin.”

The servant must therefore patiently endure calamities and seek forgiveness for his faults. Allah Most High does not command indecency, does not approve of disbelief for His servants, and does not love corruption. Yet He, glorified be He, is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of everything. Whatever He wills comes to pass, and whatever He does not will does not come to pass. Whoever Allah guides, none can lead astray; and whoever He leads astray, none can guide.

The servant’s will to do good or evil is real: he has a will to do either, the ability to do either, and he is the one who does either. Allah is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of all of this. There is no creator other than Him and no lord besides Him. Whatever He wills comes to pass, and whatever He does not will does not come to pass.

Allah has affirmed “the two wills”—the Lord’s will and the servant’s will—and has explained that the servant’s will is subject to the Lord’s will, in His words:

“Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take a path to his Lord. But you do not will unless Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.”

The Most High also says:

“It is only a reminder to all the worlds,”

“for whoever among you wills to follow the straight path.”

“But you do not will unless Allah, Lord of all the worlds, wills.”

The Most High has also said:

“Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in lofty, fortified towers. If good befalls them, they say, ‘This is from Allah.’ But if evil befalls them, they say,

---

## Page 3954

‘This is from you.’ Say, ‘All is from Allah.’ So what is the matter with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?”

“Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself.”

Some people suppose that the good and evil mentioned here mean acts of obedience and disobedience. They therefore dispute: one says, “Say, ‘All is from Allah,’” while the other says, “Good is from Allah, and evil is from yourself.” Both have misunderstood the verse, for what is meant here by good and evil is blessings and calamities, as in His words:

“And We tested them with good things and bad things so that they might return.”

That is, We tried and tested them with prosperity and adversity.

The meaning of the verse concerning the hypocrites is this: whenever something good befell them, such as victory, provision, or well-being, they would say, “This is from Allah.” But whenever something bad befell them—such as being beaten, illness, or fear of the enemy—they would say, “This is from you, O Muhammad! You are the one who brought this religion, because of which people have become our enemies and we have been afflicted with these calamities.” Allah Most High therefore said:

“So what is the matter with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?”

You only commanded them to do what is right and forbade them to do what is wrong. Whatever blessing befalls you—victory, well-being, or provision—is from Allah: a blessing He has bestowed upon you. Whatever evil befalls you—poverty, humiliation, fear, illness, or anything else of that kind—is from yourself, your sins, and your misdeeds. As He says in another verse:

“Whatever calamity befalls you is because of what your own hands have earned.”

And the Most High says:

“How is it that, when a calamity befell you, though you had inflicted twice as much, you said,

---

## Page 3955

‘Where has this come from?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’” And the Most High says:

“But if some evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, then man is indeed ungrateful.”

When calamities befall a person because of his sins and misdeeds, he is the one who has wronged himself. If he repents and seeks forgiveness, Allah grants him relief from every worry, a way out of every hardship, and provision from where he does not expect.

Committing sins is like consuming poison. If a person consumes poison, he falls ill or dies. He is the one who becomes ill, feels pain, suffers, and dies, while Allah is the Creator of all of this. He became ill because he consumed it, and he is the one who wronged himself by consuming poison. If he drinks an effective antidote, Allah restores him to health. Thus, sins are like consuming poison, and an effective antidote is like effective repentance.

The servant is in need of Allah Most High in every circumstance. Through His grace and mercy, Allah inspires him to repent; when he repents, Allah accepts his repentance. When the servant asks Him and calls upon Him, He answers his supplication. As He says:

“When My servants ask you about Me, I am indeed near. I answer the call of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me, so that they may be rightly guided.”

Whoever says that a person has no will, whether in good or evil, speaks falsely. Whoever says that he wills any good or evil independently of Allah’s will also speaks falsely. Rather, he has a will in everything he does by choice, whether good or evil, yet all of this occurs only by Allah’s will and power. Both must be believed, so that one affirms the commands and prohibitions, the promises and warnings, and the divine decree, both its good and its evil: whatever befalls the servant could never have missed him, and whatever misses him could never have befallen him.

---

## Page 3956

Whoever invokes divine decree to justify sins has no valid argument, and whoever offers it as an excuse has no acceptable excuse. Rather, such people are astray. As one scholar said of them:

“When obeying Allah, you are a Qadarī (proponent of free will); when sinning, you are a Jabrī (proponent of compulsion). You adopt whichever doctrine suits your desires.”

For when someone wrongs these people—or even merely does something they dislike, although it may be right—they do not excuse him on account of divine decree. Instead, they retaliate, whether justly or unjustly. If divine decree is a valid argument for them, it is equally valid for the others; and if it is not valid for the others, neither is it valid for them. Each of them invokes divine decree only when following his desires and disobeying his Lord, not when people harm or wrong him.

The believer, however, does the opposite: when people harm him, he considers divine decree, remains patient, and seeks Allah’s reward. When he himself does wrong, he repents and seeks forgiveness. As the Most High says:

“So be patient; indeed, Allah’s promise is true. And seek forgiveness for your sin.”

Thus, the believer patiently endures calamities and seeks forgiveness for his sins and faults. The hypocrite does the opposite: he does not seek forgiveness for his sin, but instead invokes divine decree, nor does he patiently endure what befalls him. Thus he is miserable in this world and the Hereafter, whereas the believer is happy in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah—glorified be He—knows best.

---

## Page 3957

Abū al-Abbās Ibn Taymiyya was asked about good and evil, the divine decree governing creation, and the commands and prohibitions of divine law.

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. Know that Allah is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of all things. There is no Lord besides Him and no Creator other than Him. Whatever He wills comes to pass, and whatever He does not will does not come to pass. He has power over all things and knowledge of all things.

The servant is commanded to obey Allah and His Messenger and forbidden to disobey Allah and His Messenger. If he obeys, that obedience is a blessing Allah has bestowed upon him, and he receives recompense and reward through Allah’s grace and mercy. If he disobeys, he deserves blame and punishment. Allah has the conclusive argument against him, whereas no one has any argument against Allah.

All of this occurs by Allah’s decree, predestination, will, and power. Yet He loves obedience, commands it, rewards those who practise it, and honours them. He hates disobedience, forbids it, punishes those who commit it, and humiliates them. Whatever blessings come to the servant, Allah has bestowed them upon him; whatever evil befalls him is due to his sins and acts of disobedience.

As the Most High says:

“Whatever calamity befalls you is because of what your hands have earned.”

And the Most High says:

“Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself.”

That is, whatever abundance, victory, and guidance come to you, Allah has bestowed them upon you; whatever drought, humiliation, and evil befall you are due to your sins and misdeeds. All things come to pass through His will, power, and act of creation.

---

## Page 3958

Thus, the servant must believe in Allah’s decree and predestination, and in His law and command. Whoever considers the reality of divine predestination while disregarding the commands and prohibitions, promises of reward and threats of punishment, resembles the polytheists. Whoever considers the commands and prohibitions but denies divine decree and predestination resembles the Magians. Whoever believes in both, praises Allah when he does good, seeks Allah’s forgiveness when he does wrong, and knows that all of this occurs by Allah’s decree and predestination is one of the believers.

When Adam—peace be upon him—sinned, he repented, and his Lord chose him and guided him. Iblīs, however, persisted, acted arrogantly, and invoked predestination as an excuse, so Allah cursed him and banished him. Whoever repents is like Adam, while whoever persists and invokes predestination as an excuse is like Iblīs. The blessed follow their father Adam, while the wretched follow their enemy Iblīs.

We therefore ask Allah the Magnificent to guide us to the straight path—the path of those upon whom He has bestowed His favour: the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. And Allah knows best.

---

## Page 3959

The Shaykh—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—also said:

The hadith of ‘Alī—may Allah be pleased with him—recorded in al-Sahīh recounts how the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—visited him and Fātimah at night while they were asleep and said, “Will you two not pray?” ‘Alī replied, “O Messenger of Allah, our souls are in Allah’s hand: if He wills, He retains them, and if He wills, He releases them.” The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—turned away, striking his thigh with his hand and saying:

“But man is, more than anything, prone to dispute.”

This hadith explicitly condemns those who invoke predestination to counter a command. For his words, “Our souls are in Allah’s hand,” and what follows, appeal to predestination to justify not complying with the command. Although this statement is true in itself, it cannot serve to counter the command. Rather, using it to counter the command is a form of the blameworthy disputation concerning which Allah said:

“But man is, more than anything, prone to dispute.”

Such people constitute one category of the “Qadariyyah,” and elsewhere Allah has described them as engaging in false disputation (*).

## Page 3960

A Question Concerning Predestination

Posed by a scholar from among the protected non-Muslims, who said:

O scholars of religion, a non-Muslim under your religion’s protection
Is bewildered; guide him with the clearest proof.

If my Lord has decreed my unbelief, as you claim,
Yet does not approve it from me, what recourse have I?

He called me, yet barred the door against me—is there
A way for me to enter? Explain my case to me.

He decreed my going astray, then said, “Be content with the decree.”
Yet I am not content with what brings me misery.

If, my people, I am content with what has been decreed,
My Lord does not approve my woeful affliction.

Can I be content with what my Master does not approve?
I am bewildered; show me how to dispel my perplexity.

If my Lord wills unbelief from me,
Am I disobedient in following His will?

Have I any choice to oppose His decree?
By Allah, then, cure my affliction with proofs.

Shaykh al-Islām, the shaykh, imam, learned and eminent scholar Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah, replied extemporaneously:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds.

---

## Page 3961

Your question, O man, is that of an obstinate adversary,
Disputing with the Lord of the Throne, the Maker of creation.

This is the very question with which Iblīs, the source of calamity,
Long ago disputed with the heavenly assembly.

Whoever makes himself an adversary of the All-Watchful
Will surely tumble headfirst into the pit.

Allah’s adversaries—the Qadariyyah—will all be summoned
To the Fire on the day of their return:

Whether they deny predestination, invoke it to dispute with Allah,
Or use it to argue against His Law.

The root of people’s error, in every sect,
Is probing God’s actions and asking why.

For they failed to grasp the wisdom of His acts,
And so fell into a form of pre-Islamic ignorance.

For all creation was necessarily brought into being
By the will of the Lord of creation, its Maker.

The essence of creation’s God exists of necessity,
With His attributes, likewise necessary and beginningless.

His will, His knowledge, and His power
Are inseparable from Allah’s essence—He who decrees all things.

His bringing forth, through these, whatever He wills to create
Embodies wisdom and manifold forms of mercy.

When we say that all things proceed by His will,
We do not thereby deny His unerring revelations.

Rather, the truth is that judgment belongs to Allah alone;
His are creation and the command expressed in His Law.

He is the Sovereign, worthy of praise in every circumstance;
His is the dominion, undiminished by any partner.

Whatever our Lord and God wills comes to pass;
What He does not will, no stratagem can bring about.

His power has no deficiency, and His decree
Encompasses all: nothing is excepted in this matter.

---

## Page 3962

By this I mean that all events have come to pass
Through His power and His will alone.

Our Sovereign deserves praise for all that He has willed—
Praise surpassing every commendation.

His mercy has spread throughout creation,
With manifestations of wisdom beyond the wisest minds:

Matters that bewilder the mind when it beholds
Their sublime wisdom and every wondrous thing.

We believe that Allah is mighty in His power,
His creation, and His unfailing execution of what He wills.

We affirm all this of our God,
And affirm every wisdom it contains.

This is a subject whose deniers have long failed to grasp,
Turning back in bewilderment.

To establish its truth by explaining its depths
And precisely distinguishing the truth concerning this reality

Is the highest aim of those who approach its ocean;
Yet this is difficult within the verse of this poem,

For it requires an exposition that accurately explains
The noble attributes of our Lord and God,

His most beautiful names, the rulings of His religion,
And His actions throughout this creation.

This, praise be to Allah, has become abundantly clear;
His inspiring creation with this understanding is the finest blessing.

This has been spoken of, and the written text of His Book
Offers an exposition that heals ailing souls.

Your asking, “Why did He will this?”
Is like someone asking, “Why did He exist from eternity?”

Reason rejects the very basis of that question,
And every revealed law has forbidden it.

The universe contains countless particular features, showing
Anyone with a measure of reason that they proceed from will.

---

## Page 3963

And tracing its origin through one thing after another,
Or appealing to mere possibility, is a bewildered conjecture.

There is no doubt that every effect depends
On a preceding cause that necessitates it.

The real issue concerns the causes—the causes of all you see—
And their proceeding from the Sovereign Judge through His will alone.

Your asking, “Why did God will this?”
Is what plunged human minds into the depths of a pit.

For the Magians, who affirm a creator of benefit
And a lord who brings harm into being—

Their asking about the reason behind this mystery
Entangled their forebears in the delusion of dualism.

And those heretical philosophers who maintain
That action is eternal, owing to a cause,

Sought a cause for the universe’s existence after nonexistence;
Finding none, they went grievously astray.

In every community professing a blessed, prophetic faith,
Evil began through their delving into this:

From it arose their associating partners with Allah,
And the clear proofs faded during a lapse of prophetic guidance.

It is sufficient to refute you that the excuse you seek
Is rejected by every human being’s innate nature.

You blame all those who attack you,
And heap every reproach upon them.

You bestow sincere affection upon your allies,
And hate those who oppose you, whatever their faction.

Yet in every word and deed, their position is like yours,
As the weightiest proof establishes.

Suppose you withheld blame from every disbeliever
And every misguided person who is no object of love:

You would then have to turn away from every oppressor
Who violates people’s persons, property, or honour.

---

## Page 3964

and never be angry with anyone who sheds blood,
Or steals the wealth of someone in need;

Nor one who reviles another’s guarded honour, however exalted,
Nor one who engages in illicit intercourse;

Nor one who bars people’s passage along their roads,
Nor one who spreads corruption throughout the earth;

Nor one who bears false witness, lying and fabricating,
Nor one who accuses chaste women of fornication;

Nor one who deliberately destroys crops and offspring,
Nor one who judges people in return for bribes.

Restrain your tongue from blaming anyone who spreads corruption,
And never punish anyone for a crime.

Ease the way for those who deliberately lie about their Lord—
For everyone who brings forth a fabrication—

Even if they intend to mislead those who heed them,
Seeking to corrupt humankind and then gain leadership.

Plead for the accursed Pharaoh, who transgressed
And was drowned in the sea in wrathful retribution;

And for every hardened disbeliever who associates partners with his God,
And every other tyrant who denies prophethood:

Such as ‘Ād, Nimrod, the people of Sālih,
The people of Noah, and the people of the Thicket.

Argue against Moses, and all the other prophets
Who came to revive the divine law,

For having fought people when they transgressed
And inflicted severe punishment for disobedience.

## Page 3965

Otherwise, all creatures, in every word,
Every glance of an eye or movement of a hair,
Every stroke of a hand or step of a foot,
Every motion—indeed, every moment of stillness—
Are subject to Allah’s decrees and His judgment,
Just as you are, according to the argument you have offered.

Suppose you absolve everyone who commits
Ruinous deeds, carrying this analogy through:

Can all blame possibly be lifted
From everyone for every vile deed?

Can punishment of transgressors be abandoned,
And people cease to uphold justice among their subjects,

So that no life or property is compensated with its equivalent,
And no aggressor punished in proportion to his crime?

Would people’s reason or natural disposition accept
The scoundrel’s plea: “What could I do?”

Sufficient to refute you is what afflicts the body of a human being—
A child or an insane person—and every beast:

Pain decreed, with no means of averting it;
And in whatever Allah wills lies perfect wisdom.

If He has wisdom in this, what then should be thought
Of His creating the deed and then imposing punishment?

How could it be otherwise, when some such suffering arises
As a natural consequence of the act—the servant’s own act?

Like someone who eats poison, whose eating causes death:
All of this is decreed by the Lord of creation.

## Page 3966

Thus your disbelief, O man, is like poison you have eaten;
The torment of the Fire is like a choking draught.

Do you not see that in this world an offender
Is punished, whether by divine decree or revealed law?

The Creator’s decree affords the offender no excuse;
So too in the Hereafter, without exception.

The Lord of creation’s decreeing a sin entails
His decreeing its consequences—unless repentance intervenes,

Or something akin to repentance in removing
The consequences of His servants’ wicked deeds:

Such as good deeds through which sins are erased, or an answered prayer

The evildoer’s saying, “It was decreed for me,”
Is like the wolf’s saying, “This is my nature.”

His decreeing a deed that brings retribution
Is like His decreeing all things through causes.

Does it help the blameworthy to plead
That such is their nature? Does it win pardon for their lapse?

Or are blame and punishment all the more warranted
For one whose nature is to commit atrocious evils?

So if you hope to receive an answer that might
Save you from Allah’s dreadful Fire,

## Page 3967

Then turn to the Lord of creation in humble supplication,
Seeking that He guide you to the truth.

Make your soul yield its reins to the truth, and listen;
Do not turn away from sound reflection.

Whatever truth becomes clear, never abandon it;
Do not disobey one who calls to the most upright way.

Abandon the religion of those bound by custom; do not follow it,
And turn aside from the path of the people who incurred wrath.

Do not follow anyone who has strayed from the truth;
Weigh people’s beliefs and practices impartially.

Bringing glad tidings to whoever comes with the upright faith—

And the religion of Allah’s Messenger, the best of creation.

Now has come this Gatherer, the Seal of the Prophets,
Whose universal message encompasses every good.

He conveyed from the Lord of His servants that whoever

Such is the direction servants can offer the bewildered;
But guiding him belongs to the Lord alone.

Lack of guidance among mankind does not avail
One who turns away from it; he proceeds without a valid plea.

## Page 3968

The plea of one who invokes his Lord’s decree
Only increases his torment, like an ailing woman’s plea.

As for our contentment with the decree,
We are commanded only to accept such things as calamities:

Illness and poverty, humiliation and exile,
And any harm unaccompanied by wrongdoing.

As for deeds that He dislikes us to perform,
We must not approve what He abhors merely because He wills it.

Some scholars have said: “There must be no approval
Of acts of disobedience and major sins.”

Another group says: “We are content with His decreeing,

Others say: “We accept these deeds insofar as they are attributed
To Him, but meet what pertains to us with displeasure.”

For these deeds are the Lord’s creation,
Yet, for His creatures, they are not mere acts of instinct.

Thus we accept them insofar as He creates them,
But abhor them as acts by which sin is incurred.

The accountable servant’s disobedience is his neglect
Of what his Lord commands, even though it occurs by His will.

For the Lord of creation has truly declared
That His servants will be in Hell or Paradise.

Just as they experience the like in this world;
Even beasts experience suffering and ease.

Whatever distinctions His supreme wisdom has ordained,
It has ordained with knowledge, might, and mercy.

In His might, He drives those destined for punishment
Towards torment through the means He decrees;

## Page 3969

and He guides those destined for bliss towards their bliss
Through sincere deeds performed in hope and fear.

The command of creation’s God is plainly the means
By which He leads those destined for bliss towards happiness.

For whoever is destined for happiness, His commands take effect
By making righteous deeds easy for him.

But whoever is destined for misery attains no happiness
Through command or prohibition, for misery has been decreed.

The servant cannot escape what has been decreed for him,

So take my reply and understand its meanings:
When unraveled through natural discernment,

## Page 3971

Shaykh al-Islām said:

Section

I have mentioned elsewhere that the Qadariyyah are “of three types”: “polytheistic Qadariyyah,” “Magian Qadariyyah,” and “Iblīs-like Qadariyyah.”

The first are those who acknowledge divine decree and predestination and claim that this accords with divine commands and prohibitions. They say:

“Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have associated partners with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything”—and so on, in Sūrat al-An‘ām.

“And those who associated partners with Allah said, ‘Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him’”—in Sūrat al-Nahl.

And in Sūrat al-Zukhruf:

“And they said, ‘Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them.’”

Their position ultimately leads to nullifying the revealed laws, commands, and prohibitions, while acknowledging Allah’s universal lordship over every creature, and that there is no creature but that my Lord holds it by its forelock. This frequently afflicts groups among the Sufis and the fuqarā (the poor)—whether as a belief or a state—until some of them go so far as to permit forbidden things, dispense with obligations, and abolish

---

## Page 3972

punishments, although they cannot sustain this in practice. They act upon it only when it accords with their desires, as did the Arab polytheists. Then, whenever someone’s desires are opposed, he rises to resist that opposition, transgressing all bounds and observing no limit—just as the polytheists also used to do. This approach becomes self-contradictory when human wills conflict: one person wants something, while another wants its opposite, and both wills are divinely decreed. One must therefore give precedence to one of them, to some alternative, or to each in a particular respect; otherwise, chaos necessarily follows. The adherents of this approach may go to such extremes that they identify existing things themselves with Allah, as has been discussed elsewhere.

They invoke conformity with Allah’s decretive will to justify the evil deeds committed by themselves and others, as in al-Harīrī’s statement:

“I disbelieve in a Lord who is disobeyed.”

Likewise, when one of his companions was invited by a toll collector and was told, “He is a toll collector,” he replied:

“Even if he has disobeyed the command, he has obeyed the will.”

And Ibn Isrā’īl said:

“I am now subject to whatever He chooses for me;
Thus all my deeds are acts of obedience.”

They sometimes call this “reality,” considering it the reality of lordship, the reality that actually exists, or descriptive reality. Since these people have an admixture of Christianity, and Christians have an admixture of polytheism, they followed the polytheists in invoking divine decree in opposition to the revealed law. This is despite their worshipping others besides Allah, who decreed all that exists; these people, too, have an admixture of that.

---

## Page 3973

When their heretics, who are their leaders, go further, they say:

“We worship none but Allah, since nothing exists besides Him.”

One of their leaders said, “The Christians disbelieved only because they restricted their worship.” On this basis, they sanction the worship of everything that exists and endorse the polytheists’ worship of idols and stones. Yet they regard the polytheists as falling short because they restricted worship to certain manifestations and individual entities. Clearly, such restriction is common to all polytheists: although they share in polytheism, they differ widely in the gods they worship. One worships the sun, another the moon, another al-Lāt, another al-‘Uzzā, and another Manāt, the third and last. Each takes his own desire as his god and worships whatever appeals to him. The same applies to the worship of human graves: each fixes his devotion on the likeness of someone of whom he thinks well.

The “second group of Qadariyyah” are the Magian type: those who ascribe partners to Allah in His creation, just as the former ascribed partners to Him in His worship. They say:

“The creator of good is different from the creator of evil.”

Those among them who belong to our religious community say:

“The sins that occur do not occur by the will of Allah Most High.”

Sometimes they also say, “Nor does He know of them.” They say that all the acts of living beings occur without His power or His making, thus denying His unfailing will and all-encompassing power. For this reason, Ibn ‘Abbās said:

“Divine decree is the binding thread of belief in Allah’s oneness. Whoever affirms Allah’s oneness and believes in divine decree has perfected his belief in His oneness. Whoever affirms Allah’s oneness but rejects divine decree has that belief undone by his rejection.”

They claim that this is justice, and they combine it with the negation of Allah’s attributes, which they call monotheism—just as the former call heresy monotheism. Thus both groups deviate concerning Allah’s names and attributes. This often occurs either as a belief or

---

## Page 3974

as a state of mind among many of those engaged in jurisprudence and speculative theology. This became a doctrinal belief among the Muʿtazilah and the later Shīʿah, while some earlier groups in Basra and Syria were afflicted with aspects of it. Some people may also be afflicted with it as a state of mind rather than a belief, when their reverence for divine commands and prohibitions predominates without due regard for divine decree and predestination.

Because these two groups are mutually opposed, you find the Muʿtazilah furthest removed from the Sufis. They incline towards the Jews and recoil from the Christians, equating affirmation of Allah’s attributes with the Christian doctrine of the divine Persons. Hence they are more given to censuring Christians, as al-Jāhiz and others do, whereas the former group inclines more towards Christians. Thus these concern themselves with letters and innovated discourse, just as the former concern themselves with sounds and innovated practices—a division resembling that between Jews and Christians. Most Jews are Qadariyyah in this respect: they adhere to a religious law but turn away from the reality of divine decree.

Thus you find those devoted to letters and innovated discourse, such as the Muʿtazilah, declaring their own way obligatory and every other way forbidden. They believe that severe punishment will befall anyone who opposes it. They even maintain that sinners among the adherents of religious communities will remain in Hell forever, and declare those groups within the Muslim community that depart from their way to be disbelievers. This severity, these burdens and shackles, resemble the religion of the Jews.

By contrast, you find those devoted to sound and innovated practices declaring nothing obligatory or forbidden, but merely recommending or discouraging. They exalt their way, proclaim its superiority, and encourage others to follow it, until they elevate it

---

## Page 3975

far above its proper rank. Their way is thus one of hope with scarcely any fear, whereas the former way is predominantly fear with little hope. This resembles the Christians’ excesses in the acts of worship they practise, despite casting off obligation and recommendation. Nevertheless, they perform many acts of worship and persist in them for long periods as recommended devotions. This way predominates among the philosophers, just as the former way predominates among the speculative theologians.

The third category is the Qadariyyah of Iblīs, who acknowledge that both the command and the decree come from Allah, but regard this as a contradiction. They are Allah’s adversaries, as stated in the hadith.

Such people are numerous among those devoted to discourse and practices: foolish poets and other heretics like them. An example is the saying of Abū al-‘Alā’ al-Ma‘arrī:

“Have You forbidden the deliberate taking of lives … and claimed that a return awaits them?
How little need they had of either state!” (1)

Another is the saying of one of these foolish heretics:

“He creates stars, and among them He creates moons.
He says, ‘O people, lower your eyes before them.’
You send women forth and cry, ‘You who are gathered here,
Put out the blaze!’ Yet Your own hand cast the fire.”

These and similar utterances render their speaker a disbeliever and liable to execution.

> **Footnotes:**

> 
> Time’s vicissitudes part two companions … Judge, my God, between time and me.
> Have You forbidden the deliberate taking of lives … yet sent two angels to take them?
> You claimed that they would return once more … How well they could have done without either state!

---

## Page 3976

Reflect, then, on how the sound faiths—those of the believers, the Jews, the Christians, and the Sabians—originally had no Qadariyyah among them. Rather, the Qadariyyah arose from the two false faiths: those of the Magians and the polytheists. However, the Christians and those who resembled them inclined toward the Sabians, while the Jews and those who resembled them (1)

## Page 3977

Shaykh al-Islām, the mufti of mankind and heir to the early generations, Abū al-‘Abbās Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked about people who invoke the prior divine decree as an excuse, saying:

“The matter has already been settled: the wretched are wretched, and the blessed are blessed.” They cite as evidence the words of Allah, glorified be He:

“Indeed, those for whom the best reward from Us has already been decreed will be kept far away from it.”

They maintain that Allah has decreed good and evil, that fornication is decreed for us, and that we have no power over our actions; rather, power belongs to Allah alone. They say that we guard against what has been decreed for us, that Adam did not disobey, and that whoever says, “There is no god but Allah,” will enter Paradise. They cite as evidence the Prophet’s words, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Whoever says, ‘There is no god but Allah,’ will enter Paradise, even if he commits fornication and even if he steals.”

Please explain to us the falsity of this group’s claims with decisive proofs.

He replied—may Allah Most High have mercy on him:

All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds. If these people persist in this belief, they are greater in disbelief than the Jews and Christians. For the Jews and Christians believe in divine commands and prohibitions, promises and threats, reward and punishment. Yet they have engaged in distortion and alteration, believing in some and rejecting others. As Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, saying, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others,’ and wish to adopt a way in between—”

“It is they who are

---

## Page 3978

truly disbelievers, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.”

“But those who believe in Allah and His messengers and make no distinction between any of them—to them He will grant their rewards. And Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.”

If someone who believes in some and disbelieves in others is truly a disbeliever, then what of someone who rejects everything and acknowledges neither Allah’s commands and prohibitions nor His promises and threats, but instead disregards all of this, invoking divine decree as an excuse? His disbelief is greater than that of someone who believes in some and disbelieves in others.

The falsity of these people’s claim becomes clear in several ways:

First: Each of them either considers divine decree an excuse for a person or does not. If divine decree is an excuse for a person, then it is an excuse for everyone, since all are equally subject to it. It would therefore follow that he must not condemn anyone who wrongs him, insults him, takes his wealth, corrupts his household, cuts off his head, or destroys crops and livestock. Yet all these people are liars who contradict themselves.

Each of them continually censures one person, hates another, and opposes another. Indeed, they hate, show hostility toward, and condemn the very person who challenges their views. If divine decree were an excuse for someone who commits forbidden acts and neglects obligations, they would have to refrain from censuring or hating anyone, or calling anyone a wrongdoer, no matter what he did.

It is well known that no one can act in this way. If people did so, the world would perish. Thus, their claim is demonstrably unsound according to reason, just as it constitutes disbelief according to the revealed law. They are liars and fabricators when they claim that divine decree is an excuse for a person.

Second: This would imply that Iblīs, Pharaoh, and the people of Noah

---

## Page 3979

and ‘Ād, and everyone whom Allah destroyed for their sins, would be excused. This is disbelief according to the consensus of the adherents of all religions.

(Third): This would imply making no distinction between Allah’s allies and His enemies, between believers and disbelievers, or between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell.

Allah Most High says:

“The blind and the seeing are not equal,

nor are darkness and light,

nor shade and scorching heat,

nor are the living and the dead equal.”

He Most High also says:

“Or should We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption on earth? Or should We treat those who fear Allah like the wicked?”

And He Most High says:

“Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, alike in their life and their death? How evil is their judgment!”

For Allah had already determined the destinies of all these people and recorded their decrees before creating them. Yet they are divided into those who are blessed through faith and righteous deeds, and those who are wretched through disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience. This establishes that divine decree and predestination provide no one with an excuse for disobeying Allah.

Fourth: We believe in divine decree, but we do not invoke it as an excuse. Whoever invokes divine decree as an excuse has an invalid argument, and whoever pleads divine decree offers an unacceptable excuse. Were such an argument acceptable, it would have been accepted from Iblīs and other sinners. Were divine decree an excuse for people, no creature would be punished, either in this world or in the Hereafter. And if divine decree were an excuse, no hand would be cut off from a

---

## Page 3980

thief, nor would a murderer be executed, nor would a prescribed punishment be imposed on an offender, nor would jihad be waged in Allah’s cause, nor would right be enjoined or wrong forbidden.

Fifth: The Prophet was asked about this. He said:

“There is not one of you whose place in Paradise and whose place in Hell have not already been written.” He was asked, “O Messenger of Allah, should we not then abandon deeds and rely on what has been written?” He replied, “No. Act, for everyone will be enabled to do that for which he was created.”

Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim. In another hadith in al-Sahīh, he was asked:

“O Messenger of Allah, tell us about the deeds people do and strive at: do they concern matters for which the pens have already dried and the scrolls have been rolled up, or matters they undertake anew in light of what has come to them?”—or words to that effect. He replied, “Rather, they concern matters for which the pens have already dried and the scrolls have been rolled up.” He was then asked, “What, then, is the point of deeds?” He replied, “Act, for everyone will be enabled to do that for which he was created.”

Sixth: It may be said that Allah knew all things and recorded them as they truly are. He, glorified be He, recorded that a certain person would believe and do righteous deeds, and thus enter Paradise, while another would disobey and act wickedly, and thus enter Hell. Likewise, He knew and recorded that a certain person would marry a woman and have intercourse with her, and thus have a child; that another would eat and drink, and thus have his hunger and thirst satisfied; and that another would sow seeds, and thus crops would grow.

Whoever says, “If I am destined to be among the people of Paradise, I will enter it without righteous deeds,” makes a false and self-contradictory statement. For Allah knew that he would enter Paradise through his righteous deeds. If he were to enter it without deeds, that would contradict what Allah knew and decreed.

---

## Page 3981

A comparable example is someone who says, “I will not have intercourse with a woman. If Allah has decreed that I should have a child, it will be born.” Such a person is ignorant, for when Allah decrees that a child will be born, He decrees that its father will have intercourse with a woman, who will then conceive and give birth. As for a child without pregnancy or intercourse, Allah has neither decreed nor recorded that.

Likewise, Allah has prepared Paradise only for the believers. Whoever thinks that he will enter Paradise without faith is mistaken. If he believes that the deeds Allah has commanded are unnecessary, and that it makes no difference whether he performs them or not, he is a disbeliever. Allah has forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers. Thus, this belief contradicts the faith whose possessor will not enter the Fire.

Section

As for His words, Most High:

“Indeed, those for whom We have already decreed the finest reward will be kept far away from it.”

Anyone for whom Allah has already decreed the finest reward must become a pious believer. Whoever is not among the believers has not had the finest reward decreed for him by Allah. Rather, when Allah has decreed something beforehand for a servant, He directs him to perform the deeds by which he will attain what was decreed for him. This is like someone for whom Allah has decreed that he will have a child: he must have intercourse with a woman and cause her to conceive. For Allah, glorified be He, has decreed both causes and their effects; both have been decreed by Him beforehand. Whoever thinks that the finest reward has been decreed by Allah for anyone without a cause has gone astray. Rather, He, glorified be He, facilitates both causes and their effects, and He has decreed both beforehand.

---

## Page 3982

Section

As for the statement, “We have no power over any of our actions,” whoever says this has spoken falsely. Allah, glorified be He, has distinguished between those who have power and ability and those who do not. He says:

“So fear Allah as much as you are able.”

And He says:

“And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by those who are able to undertake it.”

And He, Most High, says:

“Allah is the One who created you in weakness, then gave you strength after weakness, then weakness and grey hair after strength.”

Allah has affirmed that the servant has a will and performs actions. As He, Most High, says:

“For whoever among you wills to take a straight path.”

“But you do not will unless Allah, Lord of the worlds, wills.”

And He says:

“As a reward for what they used to do.”

Yet Allah, glorified be He, is the servant’s Creator and the Creator of all his power, will, and deeds. For there is no Lord besides Him and no god other than Him. He is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of all things.

---

## Page 3983

Section

As for the statement, “Unlawful sexual intercourse and other sins have been decreed for us,” this is true, but invoking it as an excuse does the speaker no good. Allah has written down His servants’ deeds, both good and evil, and their eventual misery or bliss. He has made deeds a cause of reward and punishment and has written all of this down, just as He has written down illnesses and made them a cause of death, and has written down the ingestion of poison and made it a cause of illness and death. Whoever consumes poison becomes ill or dies. Allah has decreed and written down both the cause and its consequence. Likewise, whoever commits what he has been forbidden—disbelief, wickedness, or disobedience—does what has been written down for him, yet deserves the recompense Allah has written down for whoever does such things.

These people’s appeal to divine decree to excuse their sins is of the same kind as the argument of the polytheists, about whom Allah said:

“The polytheists said, ‘Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have worshipped anything besides Him, nor would we have forbidden anything without His authority.’ Those before them did the same.”

And He, Most High, said:

“The polytheists will say, ‘Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have associated partners with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything.’”

Allah, Most High, said:

“Likewise, those before them denied the truth until they tasted Our punishment. Say, ‘Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow nothing but conjecture, and you do nothing but guess.’”

“Say, ‘The conclusive argument belongs to Allah. Had He willed, He would have guided you all.’”

---

## Page 3984

Section

Whoever says that Adam did not disobey is denying the Quran and must be called upon to repent; if he does not repent, he is put to death. For Allah said:

“Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray.”

Disobedience means contravening Allah’s revealed command. Whoever contravenes the command with which Allah sent His Messengers and revealed His Books has disobeyed, even though his action falls within what Allah has destined and decreed. These people imagined that disobedience means going beyond Allah’s decree. But this is impossible, for no created being can go beyond Allah’s decree. If disobedience meant only this, then neither Iblīs, Pharaoh, the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, nor any of the disbelievers would be disobedient either, because they all fall within Allah’s decree.

The person who says this is then beaten and humiliated. If he complains of being wronged by whoever treated him this way, he is told: “The person who did this is not disobedient, for he falls within Allah’s decree, like all other created beings.” Whoever makes this claim contradicts himself and cannot maintain a consistent position.

---

## Page 3985

Section

As for the claim, “Whoever says, ‘There is no god but Allah,’ will enter Paradise,” and the appeal to the aforementioned hadith, the response is:

There is no doubt that the Quran and Sunnah contain both promises and warnings. Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, those who unjustly consume the property of orphans are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a blazing Fire.”

Allah Most High also says:

“O you who believe, do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly, but only through trade by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you.”

“And whoever does that in aggression and injustice, We will cast him into a Fire. And that is easy for Allah.”

There are many such passages in the Quran and Sunnah. The servant must believe in both, rather than believe in some and disbelieve in others. These polytheists wanted to believe in the promises while denying the warnings. The Harūriyyah and the Muʿtazilah wanted to believe in the warnings but not the promises. Both groups were mistaken.

The position of Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamāʿah is to believe in both the promises and the warnings. Just as Allah—glorified be He—has explained that the punishment with which He threatens His servant is subject to conditions: that the servant does not repent, for if he repents, Allah accepts his repentance; and that he has no good deeds that erase his sins, for good deeds do away with

---

## Page 3986

evil deeds; and that Allah does not will to forgive him:

“Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.”

Likewise, the promise must be explained and clarified. Whoever says with his tongue, “There is no god but Allah,” yet rejects the Messenger is a disbeliever by the consensus of the Muslims. The same applies if he denies anything Allah has revealed. It is therefore essential to believe in everything the Messenger brought. If a person commits major sins, his fate rests with Allah: if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He forgives him. If he apostatizes from Islam and dies an apostate, he will be in the Fire.

Repentance wipes out evil deeds, while apostasy nullifies good deeds. Whoever has both good and evil deeds will not be wronged by Allah. Rather, whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. Allah Most High may bestow His bounty and kindness upon him through His forgiveness and mercy. Whoever dies with faith will not remain in the Fire forever. Thus, those who commit unlawful sexual intercourse or theft will not remain in the Fire forever; rather, they will surely enter Paradise. For whoever has an atom’s weight of faith in his heart will be brought out of the Fire.

Those about whom the question was asked are called the polytheistic, antinomian Qadariyyah. More reports condemning them have been transmitted than can be accommodated here. Allah—glorified and exalted be He—knows best. May Allah bless our master Muhammad, his family, and his Companions, and grant them peace. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.
