The lowest are the opposite of these: they become angry, exact retribution, and punish for their own sake, not for their Lord’s. If one of them is harmed or his desires are opposed, he becomes angry, exacts retribution, and punishes. Yet if Allah’s prohibitions are violated or His rights neglected, it does not concern him. This is the condition of the disbelievers and hypocrites.

---

## Page 4048

Between these two extremes are two further categories: “one category” becomes angry for both their Lord’s sake and their own, while “another category” inclines towards pardon concerning both Allah’s rights and their own. When Moses became angry with his people for worshipping the calf, his anger was for Allah’s sake. Regarding Allah’s rights, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, likened Abū Bakr and ʿUmar to Abraham, Jesus, Noah, and Moses, saying:

“Allah softens some men’s hearts for His sake until they become softer than milk, and makes other men’s hearts firm for His sake until they become harder than stone. You, Abū Bakr, are like Abraham and Jesus; and you, ʿUmar, are like Noah and Moses.”

As for pardoning violations of one’s own rights, that is better, although exacting retribution is permissible. Likewise, it is better to refrain from anger on one’s own behalf, although exacting retribution is permissible. As for calamities that occur by Allah’s decree, where there is no longer an offender to be punished, nothing remains but patience and submission to the decree.

The account of Adam and Moses belongs to this category. Moses reproached him for what had befallen him and his descendants. But Adam had already repented of his sin and been forgiven, and the calamity had been decreed. Thus Adam prevailed over Moses in argument.

Likewise, people may suffer calamities through the actions of sinners who have repented: for example, a disbeliever who kills a Muslim, then embraces Islam and whose repentance Allah accepts; or someone who adopts an innovation on the basis of an interpretation, then repents of that innovation; or someone who errs in exercising independent scholarly judgment or in following another’s judgment. When a person suffers harm through the actions of such people, it is akin to calamities sent from heaven, for which no retribution is sought from any human being.

---

## Page 4049

And fighting during “civil strife” falls into this category. Al-Zuhrī said:

“Civil strife broke out while the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, were still numerous. They agreed unanimously that any blood shed, property taken, or sexual inviolability violated on the basis of an interpretation of the Quran entailed no liability.”

The same applies to “fighting rebels acting on an interpretation,” whom Allah has commanded to be fought. If those upholding justice fight them, and the rebels take lives or destroy property belonging to those upholding justice, no compensation is due according to the great majority of scholars, including Abū Hanīfah, Mālik, and al-Shāfiʿī in one of his two opinions. This is also the apparent position of Ahmad’s school.

The same applies to “apostates” who acquire armed strength, kill Muslims, shed their blood, and take their property. During the wars against the apostates, the Companions agreed that, after embracing Islam, they were not liable for the lives and property they had destroyed. They had acted on an interpretation, even though their interpretation was false. Likewise, the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, transmitted from him through numerous independent chains, established that when disbelievers killed Muslims and destroyed their property, then embraced Islam, they were not liable for the lives and property they had taken. Those whose lives and property were taken had been striving in Allah’s cause: Allah had purchased their lives and property from them in exchange for Paradise. Compensation for what was taken from them therefore rests with Allah, not with those wrongdoers whom the believers fought.

If this applies to bloodshed and property, it applies all the more to violations of honour. Thus, whoever strives in Allah’s cause with his tongue—by enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, explaining the religion, conveying the commands, prohibitions, and good teachings contained in the Book and the Sunnah, exposing statements contrary to them, and refuting those who oppose the Book and the Sunnah—or through physical action, such as fighting disbelievers, then if

---

## Page 4050

he is harmed for his striving by another person’s hand or tongue, his reward for that rests with Allah. He does not seek compensation from that wrongdoer for the wrong he has suffered. Rather, if the wrongdoer repents and accepts the truth for which that striving was undertaken, repentance wipes away what preceded it:

“Tell those who disbelieve that if they desist, their past will be forgiven.”

If, however, he does not repent but persists in opposing the Book and the Sunnah, then he is opposing Allah and His Messenger. The rights violated by his sins belong to Allah and His Messenger, although the believers “also” have a right subordinate to Allah’s right. This applies when he is punished to uphold Allah’s right, so that Allah’s word may be supreme and all religion may be devoted to Allah, not merely for retribution.

If the disbelievers commit aggression against the Muslims—for example, by mutilating them—the Muslims may mutilate them as they themselves were mutilated, though patience is better. If they do so, that falls within the full scope of jihad. Praying against wrongdoing disbelievers as a class is prescribed and commanded. Qunūt (supplication during prayer), praying for the believers, and praying against the disbelievers have been prescribed.

As for praying against particular individuals, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to curse so-and-so and so-and-so, it has been reported that this was abrogated by His words:

“You have no say in the matter.”

This has been discussed at length elsewhere, in what I wrote in the citadel in Egypt. The reason is that one does not know whether Allah is pleased for a particular individual to perish; rather, he may be among those whose repentance Allah accepts. This differs from praying against them as a class: when one prays against them for something that brings honour to the religion, humiliation to its enemies, and their suppression, one is praying for what Allah loves and is pleased with. Allah loves faith, the people of faith, their ascendancy, and the humiliation of the disbelievers. Thus, this is a prayer for what Allah loves. As for praying against a particular individual for something when it is not known whether Allah

---

## Page 4051

is pleased with it, this is not enjoined. Such supplication was previously practised, but was later forbidden, for Allah may accept that person’s repentance or punish him.

Noah’s supplication for the destruction of the people of the earth came after Allah had informed him that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed. Even so, it is established in the authentic hadith concerning intercession that he will say:

“I offered a supplication against the people of the earth which I had not been commanded to offer.”

Although he had not been forbidden to make it, neither had he been commanded to do so. It would therefore have been better for him to offer only supplications that were enjoined, whether obligatory or recommended. Supplication is an act of worship, and Allah is to be worshipped only through what He has enjoined, whether obligatory or recommended. Had this supplication been commanded, it would have formed part of the law prescribed for Noah; we would then have to consider whether our law abrogated it.

The same applies to Moses’ supplication:

“Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.”

If this was a supplication he was commanded to make, it would remain to consider whether our law accords with it. The general principle in our law is that if a supplication is obligatory or recommended, it is good, and the one who offers it is rewarded. If it is forbidden, as in praying for unlawful bloodshed, it is a sin and an act of disobedience. If it is disliked, it diminishes the standing of the one who offers it. If it is permissible, with neither offering it nor refraining from it preferable, it counts neither for nor against him. Such is the matter. And Allah, glorified be He, knows best.

---

## Page 4052

Section

There are two groups: those who journey towards Allah solely through aspiration, love, and drawing ever nearer to Him, without regard for the commands and prohibitions revealed by Allah. Their path culminates in self-effacement in recognizing Allah’s oneness in lordship. They speak of undifferentiated awareness and total self-effacement in recognizing His oneness in lordship, but do not reach the “second distinction.” They say that someone in this state of self-effacement neither regards a good deed as good nor an evil deed as evil, and they make this the ultimate goal of the spiritual path.

The other group distinguishes between what they approve and disapprove of, what they love and hate, and what they command and forbid—but according to their own wishes, loves, and desires, not according to the Book revealed by Allah.

Both groups follow their own desires without guidance from Allah. Neither group has truly fulfilled the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. For truly fulfilling the testimony to Allah’s oneness requires that one love only for Allah’s sake, hate only for Allah’s sake, give allegiance only for Allah’s sake, and oppose others only for Allah’s sake; that one love what Allah loves, hate what He hates, command what Allah has commanded, and forbid what Allah has forbidden; and that you place your hope in Allah alone, fear Allah alone, and ask of Allah alone. This is the religion of Abraham, and this is the Islam with which Allah sent all the messengers.

---

## Page 4053

And self-effacement in this is the “self-effacement” commanded and taught by the messengers. It means forsaking worship of anything besides Allah by worshipping Him, obedience to anything besides Him by obeying Him, reliance on anything besides Him by relying on Him, and hope in and fear of anything besides Him by placing one’s hope in Him and fearing Him. One thus remains with the True One, without regard for creation, as Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir said:

“Be with the True One without regard for creation, and with creation without regard for yourself.”

Truly fulfilling the testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah entails that obedience to him is obedience to Allah, and pleasing him is pleasing Allah. Allah’s religion consists of what His Messenger commanded: lawful is what he made lawful, unlawful is what he made unlawful, and religion is what he prescribed. Hence Allah required those who claim to love Him to follow His Messenger, saying:

“Say, ‘If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you.’”

He guaranteed that Allah would love those who follow His Messenger, saying: “Allah will love you.”

Whoever follows him in this way comes to desire only what Allah and His Messenger love, and to dislike only what Allah and His Messenger dislike. Such a person is loved by the True One, as He said:

“My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him. When I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he grasps, and his foot with which he walks. Through Me he hears, through Me he sees, through Me he grasps, and through Me he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give to him; if he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely grant him refuge. I have never hesitated over anything I am to do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike distressing him, yet he must undergo it.”

---

## Page 4054

Such a person, then, is loved by the True One. Whoever follows the Messenger is loved by the True One, drawing near to Allah through the obligatory and voluntary acts to which the Messenger called. Clearly, someone like this loves obedience to Allah and His Messenger and hates disobedience to them. All obligatory and voluntary acts of worship are loved by Allah and His Messenger; they contain neither unbelief nor sinful defiance. The Lord Most High loves this person because he does what the True One loves, for a person is recompensed in kind. As he continually draws near to the True One through the voluntary acts He loves, after fulfilling the obligations, the True One loves him, for he has devoted his utmost efforts to what the True One loves. Thus, the True One loves him with a perfect love unattainable by those who draw less near to Him through the things He loves. He comes to know and act through the True One: through Him he hears, through Him he sees, through Him he grasps, and through Him he walks.

As for someone who does not regard a good deed as good or an evil deed as evil, he no longer distinguishes between “two kinds” of things: those loved by the True One and those hated by Him. Rather, he regards everything created as loved by the True One, just as it is willed by Him.

Their fundamental position is that of Jahm ibn Safwān of the Qadariyyah. They are thus among the extreme Jahmī determinists concerning divine decree, even though, concerning the divine attributes, they declare the Jahmiyyah who deny those attributes to be unbelievers. Such is the case with Abū Ismāʿīl al-Ansārī, author of “Manāzil al-Sāʾirīn” (The Stations of the Wayfarers), “Dhamm al-Kalām” (The Censure of Speculative Theology), “al-Fārūq” (The Criterion), “Takfīr al-Jahmiyyah” (Declaring the Jahmiyyah Unbelievers), and other works. In affirming the divine attributes, he stands in the strongest opposition to the Jahmiyyah and those who deny the attributes. Yet concerning actions and divine decree, his position agrees with that of Jahm and his followers among the extreme determinists. This is also the position of al-Ashʿarī and his followers, and of many jurists who follow the four imams, as well as many scholars of hadith and Sufis.

---

## Page 4055

For these people affirmed divine decree in agreement with the early generations and the majority of the imams—and they were correct in doing so. They opposed the denial of divine decree by the “Qadariyyah” among the Muʿtazilah and others. Yet in doing so, they followed the approach of Jahm ibn Safwān and his followers, claiming that all things proceed solely from a will that selects one of two equivalent alternatives without a reason.

They said, “Will, love, and approval are the same.” In this they agreed with the Qadariyyah, for both the Jahmiyyah and the Muʿtazilah maintain that an agent possessing power and choice gives preference to one of two equivalent alternatives without a determining factor. Both also maintain that there is no distinction between will, love, and approval.

The “Qadariyyah” then said, “It is known from the Quran, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the early generations that Allah loves faith and righteous deeds, does not love corruption, does not approve disbelief for His servants, and hates disbelief, sinful defiance, and disobedience.”

They said, “It therefore follows that every act of disobedience that occurs takes place without His will or volition, just as it takes place contrary to His command, love, and approval.” They also said, “His love and approval of His servants’ deeds mean His commanding those deeds; likewise, His willing them means His commanding them.” Thus, according to them, He never wills anything other than what He commands. These people then proceeded to give distorted interpretations of the Quranic passages concerning His willing everything that happens and His creation of His servants’ actions.

The Jahmiyyah and their followers among the Ashʿariyyah and others like them said, “It is known from the Quran, the Sunnah, and consensus that Allah is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of everything. He creates only through His power and will: whatever He wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen. Everything that exists is

---

## Page 4056

brought into being by His will and power, and He is its Creator; this applies equally to His servants’ actions and to everything else.”

They then said, “Since He wills everything that occurs, and will is the same as love and approval, He loves and approves of everything that occurs.” They also said, “Whatever disbelief, sinful defiance, and disobedience exists, Allah approves of it and loves it, just as He wills it.”

They were then told: Yet He, Exalted is He, has said:

“He does not love corruption,”

and:

“Nor does He approve disbelief for His servants.”

They replied, “This is equivalent to saying that He does not will corruption and does not will disbelief for His servants. This admits of two interpretations.”

The first is that this applies specifically to those who have not committed disbelief or corruption. According to them, there is no doubt that Allah neither wills nor loves what has not occurred. Thus they said, “It means that He does not love corruption for His believing servants, nor does He approve of it for them.”

What their position actually entails is that Allah likewise neither loves nor approves of faith on the part of the disbelievers. In their view, love and approval, like will, relate to what has occurred, not to what has not occurred—whether it is commanded or forbidden, and whether it is among the causes of His servants’ happiness or misery. They hold that Allah loves whatever disbelief, sinful defiance, and disobedience has occurred, and does not love whatever faith and obedience has not occurred, just as He willed the former but not the latter.

As for the second interpretation, they said, “He does not love corruption as religion, nor does He approve of it as religion.” What this statement actually means is that He does not will it as religion. For when He wills something to occur in a particular manner, He does not will it to occur otherwise; and when He wills something to occur together with something else

---

## Page 4057

He does not will it to occur on its own. For when He wills to create Zayd from ʿAmr, He does not will to create him from someone else. When He wills to send down rain through which the earth produces vegetation, He wills to send it down in that particular manner. When He wills that a group of people travel by sea, with some drowning, others surviving, and others making a profit, He wills precisely that combination. The same applies to faith and disbelief: He has joined faith with bliss for its adherents, and disbelief with punishment for its adherents. Yet, in their view, He does not make anything a cause of anything else or create anything for a wise purpose; rather, He merely places one thing alongside another.

In their view, He places happiness alongside faith, not through it, just as they say that He creates satiety at the time of eating, not through eating. Thus, the religion He has commanded is that with which He has joined its adherent’s happiness in the Hereafter. As for disbelief, sinful defiance, and disobedience, they hold that He loves and approves of them just as He wills them. However, He does not love them together with happiness for the person who commits them. Hence, He does not love them as religion, just as He does not will them as religion accompanied by happiness for their adherent.

This is the vision beheld by those who experience self-effacement in affirming the oneness of divine lordship. They saw that the Lord, Exalted is He, created everything by His will and knew that whatever He willed would come to pass. In their view, nothing has a cause or a wise purpose; rather, all events occur by will.

Now, Jahm ibn Safwān and those who deny the divine attributes among the Muʿtazilah and others like them do not affirm a will subsisting in His essence. Rather, they either deny it, interpret it as meaning creation and command, or say, “He brought into being a will without a locus.”

As for those who affirm the divine attributes, such as Ibn Kullāb, al-Ashʿarī, and others—among those who affirm

---

## Page 4058

the attributes, but affirm only one individual instance of each—affirm only a single will relating to every event, one particular hearing relating to everything heard, one particular sight relating to everything seen, and one and the same speech encompassing every kind of speech, as is known concerning their doctrine.

These people say:

All events proceed from that one, numerically single will, which gives preference to one of two equivalent alternatives without any determining factor. This will is also love, approval, and so forth.

When these people behold this, they no longer distinguish between events in terms of goodness and badness, except insofar as they accord with a person’s wishes or run counter to them. Whatever accords with what he wants and loves is good in his eyes, and whatever runs counter to that is bad in his eyes. Thus, in reality, there is no good deed that Allah loves and no evil deed that He dislikes, except in the sense that a good deed is accompanied by pleasure for its doer, and an evil deed is accompanied by pain for its doer, without any distinction whatsoever relating to Him or to the deeds themselves.

For this reason, these people affirm neither good nor bad—not in the sense of what accords with natural disposition or runs counter to it. Goodness and badness as defined by religious law are what indicate to the person concerned that doing something may bring him pleasure or cause him pain. Hence, in their view, Allah may command anything, even disbelief, sinful defiance, and disobedience, and may prohibit anything, even faith and the affirmation of His oneness. Anything He has commanded may be abrogated by anything He has prohibited.

In their view, nothing in existence remains good or evil, good or bad, except in this respect. Thus, there is neither harm nor benefit in existence; and benefit

---

## Page 4059

and harm are relative matters: what harms one person may benefit another. As the saying goes:

“One people’s misfortunes are another people’s gains.”

Since this was the reality of the position they believed in and perceived, they divided into two groups.

One group, consisting of adherents of speculative theology and rational opinion, acknowledged the distinction based on natural disposition. They said: “There is nothing beyond this distinction based on natural disposition; there is no distinction relating to Allah whereby He loves this and hates that.”

For some of them, the promise of reward and the threat of punishment lose their force, either because they subscribe to irjāʾ or because they suppose that these serve people’s worldly interests by establishing justice, as some philosophizers maintain. Such a person consequently recognizes no distinction between one deed and another except what he himself loves or hates. Whatever he loves becomes the good that ought to be done, and whatever he hates becomes the bad that ought to be avoided.

This is the condition of many adherents of speculative theology and rational opinion who follow the views of Jahm, al-Ash‘arī, and others like them concerning divine decree. You find that their love and hatred, loyalty and enmity ultimately rest on nothing but their own desires and wishes. This is the distinction based on natural disposition.

Those among them who believe in the promised reward may perform their obligations and avoid what is forbidden, but they do so for the natural pleasures in the Hereafter associated with these—eating, drinking, and sexual intercourse. These people deny love of Allah and the pleasure of looking upon Him. In their view, when it is said that

---

## Page 4060

the servants take pleasure in looking upon Him, this means that, when they look upon Him, He creates for them pleasures in created things which they enjoy—not that looking upon Allah itself gives rise to pleasure. More than one of them has stated this, including Abū al-Ma‘ālī in his Nizāmiyyah Epistle. To count this among the secrets of monotheism belongs to the polytheism of what these deniers call monotheism, not to the secrets of the monotheism with which Allah sent the messengers and revealed the Scriptures. For love arises only from something in the beloved that the lover loves. Yet, in their view, there is nothing in existence that the Lord loves except in the sense that He wills it, and He wills every event that occurs. Nor, in their view, is there anything in the Lord that the servant loves. Rather, the servant loves only what he desires, and desires only natural things agreeable to his disposition. According to them, nothing agrees with his disposition except bodily pleasures such as eating, drinking, and sexual intercourse.

The second group—the Sufis whose spiritual journey culminated in this perception—recognized the distinction based on natural disposition. Yet their spiritual path was founded upon abandoning this distinction and renouncing the self’s gratifications and desires, wanting nothing for themselves. In their view, anyone who seeks something to eat or drink in Paradise is merely seeking his own desires and gratification. They regard all this as a deficiency incompatible with true annihilation in affirming the oneness of Lordship: it is remaining attached to the self and its gratifications.

In their view, all the spiritual stations—reliance upon Allah, love, and so forth—are merely stages for those who adhere to the revealed law as they journey toward reality itself. Once they witness the oneness of Lordship, they regard these stations as defects in relation to that reality, either because of deficient knowledge and witnessing, or because this amounts to defending

---

## Page 4061

the self and seeking its gratifications. For someone who perceives that the Lord loves, approves of, and wills everything in existence sees no difference between one thing and another, except that some things afford certain people gratification through pleasure they experience, while others cause certain people pain. Whoever has this perception is certain that anyone who distinguishes between one thing and another does so only because of deficient knowledge and witnessing of Allah as the Lord of everything, who wills everything and—according to them—loves everything. The distinction he makes relates only to his own gratification and desires, so he is seeking his own gratification and defending himself. In their view, this is a defect and a fault.

Thus, in their view, everyone who makes distinctions is deficient either in knowledge and witnessing or in purpose and will. Both are defects. This contrasts with someone whose self is annihilated in witnessing Lordship: according to them, he witnesses everything in existence as proceeding through Allah’s will, love, and approval, without distinguishing between one thing and another. He therefore neither regards a good deed as good nor an evil deed as evil, as the author of Manāzil al-Sā’irīn stated.

Hence the statement transmitted from al-Dhabīlī and Abū Yazīd:

“If you see the people of Paradise enjoying its delights and the people of the Fire being tormented in the Fire, and a distinction arises in your heart, you have departed from the reality of reliance upon Allah”—or he said, “from the affirmation of Allah’s oneness which is the foundation of reliance upon Him.”

It is well known that an animate being cannot remain perpetually without this distinction; rather, it is indispensable. Such a being inclines toward necessities such as food and drink. In the state of annihilation, however, a person may be wholly absorbed in that perception. Nevertheless, he must incline toward things he needs and therefore desire them, and recoil from things that harm him and therefore dislike them. This is a distinction rooted in natural disposition, from which no human being is free.

---

## Page 4062

Yet they may acknowledge distinctions concerning necessities without which a person cannot survive, such as food, clothing, and the like. Thus, in this world and the Hereafter, they content themselves with indispensable food and clothing, regarding this renunciation as the ultimate goal. They renounce everything in the sense that they neither desire nor dislike it, neither love nor hate it. Their renunciation of mosques is no different from their renunciation of taverns. Hence, when a leading shaykh among them arrives in a town, he begins by visiting the prostitutes in the taverns, saying:

“How are you faring under Allah’s decree?”

For in this state of witnessing, he sees no distinction between mosques, churches, and taverns, or between those who pray, enter the state of consecration for pilgrimage, and recite the Quran, and disbelievers, highway robbers, and those who associate partners with the Most Merciful.

Undoubtedly, their annihilation and their loss of awareness of “divinity and prophethood”—the testimony that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, together with the distinctions this entails—stem from deficiencies in knowledge, witnessing, faith, and affirmation of Allah’s oneness. They have witnessed one attribute of the Lord while losing awareness of another. This is a deficiency.

They may also consider witnessing the Essence in abstraction from the attributes to be more perfect. They say:

“Witnessing the acts, then witnessing the attributes, then witnessing the Essence in abstraction.”

They may assign the first to the self, the second to the heart, and the third to the spirit. They regard this deficiency in their faith, knowledge, and witnessing as the ultimate goal. Thus they resemble the Jahmiyyah, who deny the attributes, in affirming an essence devoid of attributes and saying:

“This is perfection.”

But the former maintain that the attributes do not exist in external reality, and thus say that they witness their nonexistence, whereas the latter affirm their existence in

---

## Page 4063

external reality as a matter of knowledge and belief, but they say:

“Perfection lies in losing awareness of them.”

They do not witness their nonexistence, but neither do they witness their existence. This is a grave deficiency and profound ignorance. First, they have witnessed things contrary to their actual reality, for an essence stripped of attributes has no existence in external reality. Second, what Satan seeks from such a person is the adoption of Jahmī doctrine and the denial of the attributes. In lacking knowledge and awareness of their existence, he agrees with the Jahmī who believes that they do not exist.

Suppose one person says, “I believe that Muhammad is not a messenger,” while another says, “Although I know that he is a messenger, I lose all awareness of his messengership, neither remembering it nor witnessing it.” The latter is a disbeliever just like the former. For disbelief is the failure to affirm the Messenger’s truthfulness, whether or not this is accompanied by a belief that he is lying. Indeed, it also includes failing to acknowledge what he brought and to love him.

Thus, whoever compels his heart to lose awareness of Allah’s attributes—although he knows them as he knows His Essence—and compels his heart to witness an essence stripped of attributes has compelled his heart to remain deprived of what belief in the attributes is meant to achieve. This is among the gravest forms of misguidance.

Someone who experiences annihilation in affirming Allah’s oneness in lordship may suppose that, if he witnesses nothing but the Lord’s action within him, he incurs no sin. In this, such people are like someone who consumes deadly poisons and says:

“I witness that Allah is the One who fed this to me, so it will not harm me.”

This is profound ignorance, for sins and evil deeds harm a person far more than poisons do, and his witnessing that Allah is the One who does this

---

## Page 4064

does not ward off their harm. If it did, Allah’s prophets and His pious allies would have been better able to attain this witnessing and thereby shield themselves from the harm of sins.

Some of these people imagine that if the True One grants them a spiritual state through which they can exercise power, together with unveiling, He will not hold them accountable for how they exercise that power. This is like imagining that if He grants someone dominion, He will not hold him accountable for how he exercises it. Yet the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“O Allah, none can withhold what You give, and none can give what You withhold; nor can good fortune avail its possessor against You.”

He thus explained that although Allah is the One who gives and withholds, a fortunate person’s good fortune does not benefit him; only faith and righteous deeds benefit him.

This is a fundamental principle concerning which error has led many people astray. Indeed, many of these people have gone so far as to claim that Allah’s pious allies fight His prophets and assist His enemies, and that they are commanded to do so. This is a satanic command pertaining to the divine decree. Hence some of them say:

“The disbelievers have protectors among Allah’s allies, just as the Muslims have protectors among Allah’s allies.”

Many of them imagine that the Companions of the Portico fought against the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, during one of his campaigns, and that he said:

“O my companions, are you abandoning me and leaving me?”

They replied, “We are with Allah. Whoever is with Allah, we are with him.”

They deem it permissible to fight the prophets and kill them. As one of their well-known shaykhs who lived in Syria said, “If I killed seventy prophets, I would not be in the wrong.” For in their witnessing, nothing is beloved to Allah, pleasing to Him, or willed by Him except what actually occurs. Whatever occurs, Allah loves it and is pleased with it; whatever does not occur, Allah neither loves it nor is pleased with it.

---

## Page 4065

and what occurs follows the decree, in accordance with Allah’s will and power: whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. Thus, they side with whoever prevails, because the decree is on the victor’s side, and whatever is decreed is, in their view, beloved to the True One. If the disbelievers prevail, they side with them; if the Muslims prevail, they side with them. If the Messenger is victorious, they side with him; but if his Companions are overcome, they side with the disbelievers who defeated them.

Most of those who reach this point do not acknowledge the threatened punishment of the Hereafter. For anyone who acknowledges that punishment and that it awaits the disbelievers cannot assist them and ally himself with them in conduct that incurs it. They may, however, claim that this punishment is waived altogether, or that it is waived for anyone who witnesses Allah’s oneness in lordship and abides in this reality of divine decree. Some of their shaykhs, including the aforementioned shaykh and others, maintain this.

Thus, these people, who witness nothing but the decree and acknowledge nothing beyond it except what is likewise decreed—the bliss of the obedient and the punishment of the disobedient—neither enjoin right nor forbid wrong, nor strive in Allah’s cause. They do not even pray to Allah to grant the believers victory over the disbelievers. Indeed, if one of them sees someone praying for this, he says: “The spiritual pauper, the realized adept, the gnostic—what concern is it of his? Allah does whatever He wills and grants victory to whomever He wishes.”

For he regards everyone as alike in relation to Allah and in relation to himself as well. He has no interest in either side’s victory, whether on account of his Lord—since, in his view, there is no distinction between the two before Allah Most High—or on his own account, since his personal advantages are not diminished when the disbelievers gain ascendancy; indeed, for many of them,

---

## Page 4066

their worldly advantages are greater when disbelievers, hypocrites, and wrongdoers gain ascendancy, so their desire for this is stronger. Most of the protectors who accompany them belong to this category: they obtain advantages under their ascendancy that they would not obtain under the ascendancy of the believers. Their devils love these blameworthy advantages and urge them to pursue them. The devils address them with commands, prohibitions, and unveilings that they imagine come from Allah. They believe that Allah Himself has commanded and forbidden them, and that they have received unveilings like those granted to Allah’s pious allies, whereas all of this comes from devils.

They do not distinguish between states that come from the Most Merciful and those that come from devils, because this distinction depends on recognizing that the Lord Most High Himself distinguishes between them. In their view, however, there is no distinction on Allah’s part between any of the things that occur: there is only sheer will, encompassing everything alike, so He neither loves anything nor hates anything.

This is why these people participate in the same kind of listening sessions, which stir the love, ecstasy, and spiritual experience within their souls. Such listening arouses each person’s love and desire, yet their desires differ, for they have not united upon loving what Allah and His Messenger love. According to their fundamental position, whatever the True One decrees and brings about is what He loves.

When their desires differ in ecstasy, the desires of their devils differ as well. One of them may kill another by means of his devils, because they are stronger than the other’s devils. He may also strip him of his state—the power to exert influence and the unveilings attained through their devils. His devils will have fled from the other’s devils, leaving him weakened and stripped of his state, like a king whose supporters have been taken away, leaving him abased and without a kingdom.

---

## Page 4067

Thus, many of these people resemble tyrannical kings who are hostile to one another: some are killed, some captured, and some defeated. One may capture another, who then remains under his control; another may have his state stripped away by someone else and be left without any state, like a defeated king. All of this stems from the fundamental doctrine of the Jahmiyyah, who take determinism in matters of divine decree to extremes.

Only one who affirms that Allah loves certain things and hates others, is angry at some, rejoices in some, and is displeased with others—as the messengers have reported and the scriptures have declared—can escape all of this. Such a person testifies that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. He knows that the oneness of Allah which the messengers were sent to proclaim means worshipping Allah alone, without any partner: Allah is worshipped to the exclusion of everything else.

Worship of Him combines perfect love for Him with complete humility before Him, as the Most High says:

“Turn to your Lord and submit to Him.”

His heart therefore turns to Allah and submits to Him, and he follows the faith of Abraham, inclining to the truth:

“And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while doing good and follows the faith of Abraham, inclining to the truth? And Allah took Abraham as a close friend.”

He knows that whatever Allah and His Messenger command, Allah loves and is pleased with; and whatever He forbids, He hates and prohibits, and He abhors and is displeased with those who do it. Thus, he comes to recognize the distinction made by the True One, Most High. He knows that Allah Most High loves to be worshipped alone, without any partner, and hates those who set up rivals to Him, loving them as they love Allah—even if they acknowledge His oneness in lordship, like the polytheists of

---

## Page 4068

the Arabs and others. He also knows that the doctrine of these Qadariyyah—the determinist Jahmiyyah, who are absorbed in contemplating the oneness of lordship—is essentially of the same kind as the claim of the polytheists who said:

“Had Allah willed, neither we nor our fathers would have associated partners with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything.”

Allah Most High says:

“Likewise, those before them denied the truth until they tasted Our punishment. Say, ‘Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow nothing but conjecture, and you do nothing but guess.’”

“Say, ‘To Allah belongs the conclusive argument. Had He willed, He would have guided you all.’”

These polytheists rejected the commands and prohibitions with which the messengers were sent, and rejected the oneness of Allah that consists in worshipping Him alone, without any partner. Yet they acknowledged His oneness in lordship and that Allah is the Creator of everything. Thus, in their view, no distinction remained on Allah’s part between what is commanded and what is forbidden.

They therefore said:

“Had Allah willed, neither we nor our fathers would have associated partners with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything.”

This is true: had Allah willed that this should not happen, it would not have happened. But how does this help them? All it establishes is that this association of partners with Allah and this prohibition occurred by divine decree. It does not follow that something decreed is therefore loved by Allah and pleasing to Him. They have no knowledge that Allah commanded it, loved it, or was pleased with it. Rather, they rely on nothing but conjecture and guesswork. If they invoke divine decree as an argument, divine decree is universal, not peculiar to their situation.

If they say, “We love this and resent that, so we distinguish according to our natural inclinations, since there is no distinction on the part of the True One,” the reply is: “You have no knowledge that there is no distinction on the part of Allah Most High.” Those Jahmiyyah who affirm the revealed law say that the established distinction is that the oneness of Allah

---

## Page 4069

is coupled with bliss, while associating partners with Him is coupled with punishment. This is the distinction brought by the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. In their view, it amounts to Allah’s knowledge of what will happen and His informing us of it. For these people, the distinction does not rest on His loving the one and hating the other.

They agree with the polytheists in some of what they say, not all of it, just as the Qadariyyah within this Muslim community—who are the Magians of this community—agree with the Magians proper in some of what they say, not all of it. Yet the Messenger called them to worship Allah alone, without any partner; to love Allah rather than anything besides Him; and to hold Allah and His Messenger dearer than everything else.

Love depends on the reality of its object. If the beloved is not in himself worthy of being loved, it cannot be right to command love for him, let alone require that he be dearer to us than everything else.

If it is said that “love for Him” means loving to worship and obey Him, the reply is that loving worship and obedience depends on loving the One who is worshipped and obeyed. Whoever is not loved in himself, worshipping and obeying him will not be loved. Thus, people hate obeying someone whom they hate. While hating him, they cannot love obeying him except for some other end that they love, such as a reward he gives them for their obedience. What they truly love, then, is that reward. Allah and His Messenger would therefore not be dearer to them than everything else, except in the sense that the reward they receive from among created things is dearer to them than anything else.

Loving that reward depends on being aware of it, for it is impossible to love something of which one is unaware.

If it is said: “They have been promised that, in return for loving Allah and His Messenger, they will be given the best of the created things they love,”

---

## Page 4070

the reply is: “In your view, loving Allah and His Messenger means nothing but loving that reward. Yet one is not aware of that reward so as to love it.”

If it is said: “Rather, when the one who says, ‘No other is loved except for his own sake,’ says, in effect, ‘If you obey me, I will give you the greatest thing you love,’ the recipient comes to love the one commanding him,” the reply is: “That is not so. His heart remains devoid of love for the one commanding him; it is attached only to the reward promised for his work. He is like workers who earn their wages through building, sewing, weaving, and other occupations. They may not know their employer, or may not love him, and have no interest in him personally. Their interest lies only in the payment they love.”

This is the basis of the position of the Jahmiyyah, the Qadariyyah, and the Muʿtazilah who deny love for Allah Most High. Hence the Muʿtazilah and their followers among the Shīʿah say that knowing Allah is obligatory because it serves as lutf (an aid) in fulfilling duties established by reason. Thus they made the greatest knowledge subordinate to what they supposed reason made obligatory. They deny loving Allah and looking upon Him, let alone the delight of looking upon Him.

Ibn ʿAqīl, much of whose discourse contained elements of Muʿtazilite thought, heard a man say: “O Allah, I ask You for the delight of looking upon Your Face.” He said: “Sir, suppose He has a Face—would you then take delight in looking upon Him?”

Yet this wording is transmitted from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith narrated by al-Nasāʾī and others from ʿAmmār, reporting that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in supplication:

“O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive so long as life is better for me, and cause me to die when death is better for me. O Allah, I ask You to grant me fear of You in private and in public. I ask You for truthful speech in anger and contentment. I ask You for moderation in poverty and wealth. I ask You for bliss that never runs out, and joy that never ceases. And I ask You for

---

## Page 4071

contentment after the decree, and a life of comfort after death. I ask You for the delight of looking upon Your noble Face and the longing to meet You, without any harmful affliction or any trial that leads astray. O Allah, adorn us with faith and make us guides who are themselves rightly guided.”

This wording has also been transmitted from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, through another chain—I believe it is narrated by Zayd ibn Thābit. Its meaning is also found in the authentic hadith narrated by Suhayb from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, a caller will proclaim: ‘O people of Paradise, Allah has made you a promise that He wishes to fulfil for you.’ They will say: ‘What is it? Has He not brightened our faces, made our scales heavy, admitted us to Paradise, and protected us from the Fire?’ He said: ‘Then He will remove the veil, and they will look upon Him. Nothing He has given them will be dearer to them than looking upon Him. This is the increase.’”

This refers to His words:

“For those who do good is the best reward—and more.”

Thus, he stated that nothing among the blessings they have been given is dearer to them than looking upon Him. If looking upon Him is the dearest of all things to them, it follows that He Himself is the dearest of all things to them. Otherwise, looking upon Him would not be their most cherished form of bliss. For love of seeing follows love of what is seen; the sight of something that is neither loved nor hated in itself cannot be dearer to a person than every form of bliss.

In sum, denial of the vision of Allah, of love, and also of divine speech is well known in the teachings of the Jahmiyyah, the Mu'tazilah, and those who agree with them. The Ash'ariyyah and their followers agree with them regarding

---

## Page 4072

the denial of love, but differ from them in affirming the vision of Allah. Yet the vision they affirm has no reality.

The first person known in Islam to have denied that Allah speaks and that Allah loves His servants was al-Ja'd ibn Dirham. Thus, he denied that Allah had taken Abraham as an intimate friend or spoken directly to Moses. Khālid ibn 'Abd Allāh al-Qasrī therefore offered him as a sacrifice, saying:

“Offer your sacrifices, O people! May Allah accept your sacrifices, for I am sacrificing al-Ja'd ibn Dirham. He claimed that Allah did not take Abraham as an intimate friend and did not speak directly to Moses. Exalted is Allah, far above what al-Ja'd says!”

Then he descended and slaughtered him.

As for the Sufis, they affirm love; indeed, nothing is more evident among them. The very foundation of their path is will and love. Affirmation of the love of Allah is well known in the statements of their early and later figures, just as it is established by the Quran, the Sunnah, and the agreement of the early generations.

Love is a general category encompassing many kinds. Every worshipper loves what he worships. Thus, the polytheists love their gods, as Allah Most High says:

“Among people are those who take others besides Allah as equals, loving them with a love like that for Allah. But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.”

There are two interpretations of this. (The first): They love them as the believers love Allah. (The second): They love them as

---

## Page 4073

they love Allah; for He has said:

“But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.”

Thus, it cannot be said that the polytheists worship their gods as those who affirm Allah’s oneness worship Allah. Rather, they love them as they themselves love Allah, for they set their gods equal to the Lord of all worlds. As He says:

“Yet those who disbelieve set others equal to their Lord.”

And He says:

“By Allah, we were clearly misguided when we made you equal to the Lord of all worlds.”

Some who supported the first interpretation, responding to the argument for (the second interpretation), said: “The Quran commentators have said that His words, ‘But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah,’ mean that their love for Allah is stronger than the polytheists’ love for their gods.”

The reply is: No. What these commentators said contradicts your position. You say that they love these equals as the believers love Allah, yet this contradicts the believers’ having a stronger love for Allah than the polytheists have for their lords. The weakness of this interpretation is therefore clear. It is established that the believers love Allah more than the polytheists love Allah and their gods, because the latter associate others with Him in their love, whereas the believers devote all of it exclusively to Allah.

(Furthermore, in His words), “with a love like that for Allah,” the verbal noun “love” is linked to its object—the one loved—while its subject—the one who loves—is omitted. Either the intended meaning is “as Allah is loved,” without specifying who loves Him, so that it remains general and applies to both groups; but this contradicts His words:

“But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.”

Or the intended meaning is “like their love for Allah.” It cannot mean “as others love Allah,” since nothing in the passage indicates this. Their own love, by contrast, is indicated by His words:

“Among people are those who take others besides Allah as equals, loving them with a love like that for Allah.”

He thus attributes to them the love being compared

---

## Page 4074

, and likewise the love used as the standard of comparison is theirs, since the context indicates this.

If someone says, “He loves Zayd as he loves ‘Amr,” or “He loves ‘Alī as he loves Abū Bakr,” or “He loves righteous people outside his family as he loves the righteous among his family,” or if it is said, “He loves falsehood as he loves truth,” or “He loves listening to whistling and clapping as he loves listening to the Quran,” and similar expressions, the only meaning understood is that the same person loves both objects of comparison: he loves this just as he loves that. It is not understood to mean that he loves this as someone else loves that, for nothing in the wording indicates anyone else’s love at all.

The point is that love may be directed towards something taken as a god besides Allah. Allah Most High says:

“Have you seen the one who takes his own desires as his god and whom Allah has knowingly led astray?”

Whoever worships what he desires has taken his desires as his god: whatever he desires becomes his god. He does not worship the One who deserves worship, but rather worships whatever he desires. This person who takes his desires as his god has a love like that of the polytheists for their gods, or that of the calf-worshippers for the calf. This is love alongside Allah, not love devoted to Allah. It is the love of those who associate partners with Him.

Souls may claim to love Allah, while in reality their love involves associating partners with Him: they love what they desire and have made it a partner with Allah in their love. Desire may remain hidden from the soul, for your love of something makes you blind and deaf. The same applies to deeds that a person thinks he performs for Allah, while within his soul there is an association of partners with Allah that has remained hidden

---

## Page 4075

from him, while he performs them out of love of leadership, love of wealth, or attraction to a person’s appearance. Thus, they asked:

“O Messenger of Allah, a man fights out of bravery, partisan zeal, or a desire to show off. Which of these is in Allah’s cause?”

He replied: “Whoever fights so that Allah’s word is supreme is fighting in Allah’s cause.”

When many of the later Sufi ascetics began claiming love without weighing it against the standard of knowledge, the Book, and the Sunnah, an element of associating partners with Allah and following desires entered into it. Allah Most High has made love for Him entail following His Messenger. He says:

“Say, ‘If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you.’”

This is because the Messenger calls to what Allah loves. There is nothing Allah loves that the Messenger does not call to, and nothing the Messenger calls to that Allah does not love. Thus, what the Lord loves and what the Messenger calls to are inseparable; indeed, they are identical in essence, though described in different ways.

Anyone who claims to love Allah but does not follow the Messenger has made a false claim. His love is not for Allah alone. Rather, if he does love Him, it is a love tainted by associating partners with Him, for he merely follows his own desires. Such is the claim of the Jews and Christians to love Allah: had they devoted their love sincerely to Him, they would have loved only what He loves and would therefore have followed the Messenger. Since they loved what Allah hates while claiming to love Him, their love was of the same kind as that of the polytheists.

The same applies to the people of religious innovation. Whoever says that he is among those who seek Allah and love Him, yet has no intention of

---

## Page 4076

following the Messenger, doing what he has commanded, and refraining from what he has forbidden—his love is tainted by the love of the polytheists, Jews, and Christians, in proportion to the religious innovation within him. For religious innovations that have not been prescribed and are not among the things to which the Messenger called are not loved by Allah. The Messenger called to everything Allah loves: he enjoined everything good and forbade everything evil.

Moreover, complete love for Allah and His Messenger entails hating those who oppose Allah and His Messenger and engaging in jihad in His cause. Allah Most High says:

“You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day showing affection to those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred. Those are the ones in whose hearts He has inscribed faith and whom He has strengthened with a spirit from Him.”

Allah Most High also says:

“You see many of them taking the disbelievers as allies. Evil indeed is what their souls have sent ahead for them: Allah is angry with them, and they will abide in punishment forever.”

“Had they believed in Allah, the Prophet, and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. But many of them are defiantly disobedient.”

Allah Most High also says:

“You have an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘We disassociate ourselves from you and from whatever you worship besides Allah. We reject you, and enmity and hatred have arisen between us and you forever, until you believe in Allah alone.’”

Thus, He commanded the believers to follow the example of Abraham and those with him, who openly expressed enmity and hatred towards those who associated partners with Allah until they believed in Allah alone. How far removed this is from the condition of someone who regards no good deed as good and no evil deed as evil!

---

## Page 4077

And these people pursued the path of will and love in an undifferentiated manner, without holding fast to the Quran and Sunnah, just as the adherents of speculative theology and rational opinion pursued the path of reflection and inquiry without holding fast to the Quran and Sunnah. Thus, both groups fell into various errors.

As Allah Most High says:

“If guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor fall into misery.”

“But whoever turns away from My remembrance will have a life of hardship, and We will raise him blind on the Day of Resurrection.”

“He will say, ‘My Lord, why have You raised me blind when I could see?’”

“He will say, ‘Thus did Our signs come to you, but you forgot them; and thus will you be forgotten today.’”

He also says:

“This is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other paths, for they will lead you away from His path.”

And He says:

“Indeed, this Quran guides to that which is most upright.”

And He says:

“The truth has come to you from your Lord. Whoever is guided is guided only for his own good, and whoever goes astray does so only to his own detriment.”

There are many similar passages in the Quran. This principle has been discussed at length elsewhere.

It may be objected:

The one wholly absorbed in contemplating Allah’s sole lordship has witnessed that the Lord created everything. He may also be among those who affirm divine wisdom, saying: “He created all things only for a wise purpose, which He loves and approves of. He created what He hates only for the sake of what He loves.”

Those who distinguish between love and will say: A sick person wants medicine but does not love it; rather, he loves what it brings about—recovery and the removal of illness. The Lord Most High created everything by His will. He therefore wills everything He has created, as well as the wise purpose He loves. Although He does not love some of the entities and actions He has created, He loves the wise purpose for which they were created. Thus, when the one who knows Allah witnesses

---

## Page 4078

this, he too loves that things should be created for that wise purpose, and he wills and loves them just as the Truth does. Although he hates disbelief, defiance, and disobedience, whatever Allah has created of these, He has created for a wise purpose and by His will. Thus, it is willed and loved in view of its ultimate purpose, not in itself.

The answer is:

Whoever witnesses this regards as good what Allah deems good, loves, and approves of, and regards as reprehensible what Allah hates and is displeased with. Yet if Allah has created this hated thing for a wise purpose that He loves, the one who knows Allah likewise hates and detests it, just as Allah hates it, while loving the wise purpose for which it was created. His love and knowledge thus accord with Allah’s knowledge and love rather than opposing them.

Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise. He knows things as they truly are, and He is wise in what He loves, wills, and says, and in what He commands and does. If He knows that a particular action or thing possesses qualities for which it is blameworthy and deserves hatred and aversion, then it is part of His wisdom to detest and hate it. If He knows that its existence brings about a beloved and praiseworthy wise purpose, then it is part of His wisdom to create and will it for the sake of that beloved wise purpose, which is a means to bringing it about.

If it is said that this “intermediary” is loved insofar as it is a means to something loved for its own sake, and hated insofar as it possesses blameworthy qualities, this is sound. It is just as you might say that a person may hate medicine in one respect and love it in another. Likewise, many things are loved in one respect and hated in another.

---

## Page 4079

Moreover, he loves the distinction between something being harmful to a person and hateful to him in every respect, and Allah having created it for a wise purpose. Since Allah has created everything for a wise purpose of His, when the servant perceives that purpose alongside the common ground shared by all created things, this does not prevent him from perceiving the distinction between them by which Allah has distinguished the people of Paradise from the people of Hell. Rather, he must perceive this distinction within that commonality. Such perception accords with Allah’s knowledge and wisdom. And Allah knows best.

Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your relatives, wealth you have acquired, trade whose decline you fear, and homes you find pleasing are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah brings about His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.’”

He thus declares that whoever holds the things he loves dearer than Allah, His Messenger, and striving in His cause is among those threatened with punishment.

Concerning those whom He loves and who love Him, He says:

“Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble towards the believers, firm towards the disbelievers, striving in Allah’s cause and fearing no one’s reproach.”

Whoever loves Allah must therefore follow the Messenger and strive in Allah’s cause. Indeed, this is incumbent upon every believer.

Allah Most High says:

“The believers are only those who believe in Allah

---

## Page 4080

and His Messenger, then never doubt, and strive with their wealth and their lives in Allah’s cause—it is they who are truthful.” Such is the believer’s love for Allah.

As for “love involving the association of partners with Allah,” it entails neither following the Messenger nor hating and striving against His enemy. This is found among Jews, Christians, and polytheists who claim to love Allah but neither follow the Messenger nor strive against His enemy. Likewise, “adherents of religious innovations” who claim such love turn away from following the Messenger to an extent corresponding to their innovations. This stems from their love for others besides Allah. You find them among those furthest from allegiance to the Messenger’s allies, enmity towards his enemies, and striving in Allah’s cause, because of the innovations they harbour, which are a branch of associating partners with Allah.

Those among the “Sufis” who have claimed such love, and whose position on divine decree resembles that of the determinist Jahmiyyah, ultimately perceive nothing as beloved to the Lord except what has occurred and been decreed. In their view, whatever occurs of disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience is beloved to Him. Within this perception, no distinction remains between Moses and Pharaoh, between Muhammad and Abū Jahl, between Allah’s allies and His enemies, or between worshipping Allah alone and worshipping idols. Rather, all of this is alike to someone lost in contemplation of the oneness of divine lordship. He distinguishes one event from another only according to what he desires and loves.

This is the one who has taken his own desire as his god: he worships and loves only what he desires. Although he has love for Allah, he has taken rivals besides Allah whom he loves as he loves Allah, and they are

---

## Page 4081

those whom he desires. This is so as long as some love for Allah remains in him. Yet he may shed that love altogether and descend into ta‘tīl (negation of the divine), like Pharaoh and his kind, whose condition is worse than that of the Arab polytheists and others like them.

Thus, these people love without knowledge and hate without knowledge. Knowledge is what the Messenger brought, as Allah says:

“Then whoever disputes with you concerning him after the knowledge that has come to you”

This is the revealed law. Hence, spiritual masters endowed with knowledge would often counsel their disciples to follow knowledge and the revealed law. We have cited some of their statements elsewhere. For when love and aspiration are not guided by knowledge and the revealed law, they are of the same kind as the love and aspirations of the disbelievers.

These spiritual wayfarers and aspirants—the Sufis, those embracing poverty, the ascetics and worshippers who have taken the path of love and aspiration—must follow the revealed law and the knowledge inherited from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, loving what Allah and His Messenger love and hating what Allah and His Messenger hate. Otherwise, their path will lead them into branches of disbelief and hypocrisy.

Faith and love for Allah are not complete without believing the Messenger in what he conveyed and obeying him in what he commanded. Believing what he conveyed includes believing in the attributes with which Allah described Himself and with which His Messenger described Him. Whoever denies these attributes has rejected what he conveyed as false. Believing in what he commanded includes doing what he commanded, abstaining from what he prohibited, loving good deeds and hating

---

## Page 4082

evil deeds, and maintaining this distinction until death. Whoever does not regard the good that is commanded as good, and the evil that is forbidden as evil, has no faith at all.

As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in an authentic hadith:

“Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand. If he cannot, then with his tongue. If he cannot, then with his heart—and that is the weakest level of faith.”

Likewise, in the authentic hadith narrated by ‘Abd Allāh ibn Mas‘ūd, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Every prophet whom Allah sent to his people before me had devoted disciples and companions from among them who followed his sunnah and obeyed his commands. Then unworthy successors came after them, saying what they did not do and doing what they were not commanded to do. Whoever strives against them with his hand is a believer; whoever strives against them with his tongue is a believer; and whoever strives against them with his heart is a believer. Beyond that, there is not even a mustard seed of faith.”

Narrated by Muslim. Thus, the weakest level of faith is to reject evil in one’s heart. Whoever has no hatred in his heart for the evil that Allah and His Messenger hate has no faith at all.

Hence, those religious innovators who profess a general, shared love resembling the love of the polytheists are found to resent anyone who objects to any of their states. They say, “So-and-so objects, and so-and-so objects.” They may often be tried by someone who rejects both the truth and the falsehood they possess. The former thus resembles the Christian who accepts both truth and falsehood and loves both truth and falsehood, like the polytheist who loves Allah and also loves those set up as His rivals. The latter resembles the Jew who rejects both truth and falsehood and hates both truth and falsehood: he loves neither Allah nor those set up as His rivals. Rather, he is too arrogant to worship Allah, just as Pharaoh and his like were.

---

## Page 4083

This is frequently found among religious innovators, both those devoted to spiritual aspiration and those engaged in speculative theology. The former accept both truth and falsehood, resembling the Christians; the latter reject both truth and falsehood, resembling the Jews. The religion of Islam and the path of the people of the Quran and faith, however, consist in rejecting what Allah and His Messenger hate, loving what Allah and His Messenger love, affirming truth, and rejecting falsehood.

They are therefore balanced in what they affirm and love: they affirm truth and reject falsehood, love truth and hate falsehood. They affirm what is true and existent, and reject what is false and nonexistent. They love the truth that Allah and His Messenger love—the good that Allah and His Messenger have commanded—and hate the evil that Allah and His Messenger have forbidden. This is the straight path, the path of those whom Allah has blessed: the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. It is not the path of those who have incurred His wrath, who recognize the truth but neither affirm nor love it, nor that of those who have gone astray, who believe in and love that for which Allah has sent down no authority.

And (the point here) is that this polytheistic, innovated form of love is what has ultimately led these people to regard no good deed as good and no evil deed as evil. This is because they suppose that Allah neither loves anything He commands nor hates anything He forbids. In this respect, they have become like those who deny that Allah loves anything or hates anything, as is the position of the Jahmiyyah, who deny the divine attributes.

One of these people may affirm Allah’s love and pleasure, and his fundamental creed may include affirming the divine attributes. Yet when he comes to divine decree, he affirms nothing but the all-encompassing will. Among those who fell into this were

---

## Page 4084

groups among those who affirm the divine attributes, who spoke about divine decree in terms consistent with the views of Jahm and the Ashʿarīs. They thus contradicted the attributes they had affirmed, as did the author of Manāzil al-Sāʾirīn (The Stations of the Wayfarers) and others.

As for the leading Sufis and renowned early shaykhs, such as al-Junayd ibn Muhammad and his followers, and Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir and others like him, they were among the most steadfast in adhering to the commands and prohibitions, urging others to observe them, and warning against simply going along with divine decree as those associates of theirs did. This is the “second distinction” that al-Junayd discussed with his companions.

All of Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir’s teachings revolve around obeying what is commanded, abandoning what is forbidden, and patiently enduring what is decreed. He recognizes no path whatsoever that contradicts this—neither he nor the great majority of shaykhs accepted among Muslims. He warns against contemplating divine decree alone without observing the commands and prohibitions. This was the failing of those Sufis who witnessed divine decree and Allah’s oneness in lordship, but lost sight of the divine distinction taught by the religion and revealed law brought by Muhammad: the distinction between what the True One loves and what He hates, which affirms that there is no deity worthy of worship but Him.

This is among the most important matters that those who aspire to Allah and tread the spiritual path must observe. Many of the later generations deviated from it and strayed from the right path. This is truly understood only by someone who has turned his heart toward Allah, to whom the realities of things have been disclosed, and who has come to witness His universal lordship and His sustaining of all things. For if he lacks the light of faith and the Quran, through which discernment is attained, enabling him to witness Allah’s exclusive right to worship, which distinguishes between the people of monotheism and those of polytheism, between what Allah loves and what He hates, and between

---

## Page 4085

what the Messenger commanded and what he forbade—then he departs from the religion of Islam to the extent that he departs from this distinction. For universal lordship was acknowledged even by the polytheists of whom Allah said:

“Most of them do not believe in Allah without associating others with Him.”

A person only becomes a Muslim, upright in faith and devoted to Allah alone, when he testifies that there is no deity worthy of worship but Allah. He then worships Allah alone, associating no one with Him in his devotion, his love for Him, his servitude, his turning to Him, his submission to Him, his supplication to Him, or his reliance upon Him. He forms allegiances and enmities for His sake, loves what He loves, and hates what He hates. Through the truth of monotheism, the falsehood of polytheism is effaced from him.

This effacement is accompanied by an abiding devotion: his worship of anything besides Allah is effaced through his worship of Allah, thereby fulfilling his declaration, “There is no deity worthy of worship but Allah.” He thus rejects and effaces from his heart the worship of anything besides Him, while affirming and retaining in his heart the worship of Allah alone.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in an authentic hadith:

“Whoever dies knowing that there is no deity worthy of worship but Allah will enter Paradise.”

In another hadith:

“Whoever’s last words are ‘There is no deity worthy of worship but Allah’ will enter Paradise.”

He also said in an authentic hadith:

“Prompt your dying ones to say, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship but Allah,’ for this is the very essence of the religion of Islam. Whoever dies affirming it dies a Muslim.”

Allah Most High has commanded us in several places not to die except as Muslims, as in His words:

“Fear Allah as He should be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.”

The truthful one said:

“Let me die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.”

The correct of the two views is that he neither asked for death nor wished for it. Rather, he asked that, when he died, he would die as a Muslim. He thus asked for the condition, not for the event itself, just as Allah commanded this and commanded it of His close friend Abraham and of Israel. More than one scholar has explained it in this way, including Ibn ‘Aqīl and others. And Allah Most High knows best.

---

## Page 4086

And Shaykh al-Islam Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—said:

Section

Scholars of our school and others have discussed “the servant’s capacity to act”: does it accompany his action or precede it? They have treated these as two mutually contradictory positions.

Some hold that capacity exists only alongside the action. This is the predominant position among speculative theologians who affirm divine decree, including the followers of al-Ash‘arī and those who agree with them, whether from our school or elsewhere. Others hold that capacity precedes the action. This is the predominant position among those who deny divine decree, including the Mu‘tazilah and the Shī‘ah.

The former hold that power is applicable only to a single act, since it accompanies that act and is inseparable from it. The latter hold that capacity must allow for either of two opposite acts and never accompanies the action.

The Qadariyyah deviate further, for they deny that power can accompany the action under any circumstances. In their view, a cause must necessarily precede its effect and can never coincide with it, whether the cause in question is power, will, or command.

---

## Page 4087

And the correct view, as indicated by the Quran and Sunnah, is that capacity precedes the action and also accompanies it. The action is also accompanied by another capacity that is applicable to no other action. Capacity is thus of “two kinds”: a prior capacity that allows for either of two opposite acts, and an accompanying capacity that exists only alongside the action. The former makes the action possible and allows it to occur; the latter necessitates the action and ensures its occurrence.

Concerning the first, Allah Most High says:

“Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by those who are able to undertake it.”

If this capacity existed only alongside the action, Hajj would be obligatory only upon those who performed it. No one would sin by neglecting Hajj, nor would it be obligatory upon anyone before entering its state of consecration—indeed, before completing it.

Allah Most High also says:

“So fear Allah as much as you are able.”

He thus commands people to fear Him to the extent of their capacity. Had He meant the capacity accompanying the action, no one would be required to fear Allah beyond what he actually did, since that alone was accompanied by such capacity.

Allah Most High says:

“Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity.”

“Capacity” means what lies within the soul’s scope: what it can encompass and bear. If this meant the capacity accompanying the action, no one would be charged with anything beyond the action he actually performed, to the exclusion of the duties he left undone.

Allah Most High says:

“Whoever cannot find [a slave to free] must fast for two consecutive months before the two touch one another. But whoever is unable must feed sixty needy people.”

What is meant here is the capacity preceding the action. Otherwise, the meaning would be: whoever does not fast must feed sixty needy people. Feeding them would then be permissible for anyone who did not fast, and fasting would not be obligatory upon anyone until he actually performed it.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When I command you to do something, do as much of it as you are able.”

If only the capacity accompanying the action were intended, the meaning would be: “Do of it what you have done”

---

## Page 4088

so they would be commanded only to do what they had actually done.

Likewise, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿImrān ibn Husayn:

“Pray standing; if you are unable, then sitting; and if you are unable, then lying on your side.”

If the capacity accompanying the action were intended, the meaning would be, “If you do not do so,” leaving one free to choose. There are numerous similar examples. Whenever the Quran and Sunnah make an obligation conditional upon capacity, and its absence conditional upon incapacity, the capacity accompanying the action is not what is intended.
