## Page 4216

the servant would do it if he willed, since he has the power to do so, it may be imposed upon him as an obligation without dispute. Even if some call it something beyond his capacity, this is a dispute over terminology, and over whether ability can precede the act.

Section

As for his words:

“If compulsion holds true, he would be coerced …
And in your view, one coerced is excused.”

The response is:

The meaning of “compulsion” has already been explained. If compulsion means coercion, as when someone compels another and forces him to act against his will, then Allah Most High is far too majestic, exalted, and powerful to need such compulsion and coercion. Only someone unable to make another person will an action, choose it, love it, and be pleased with it resorts to this. Allah, glorified be He, has power over all things. If He wills to make the servant love and choose what he does, He makes him so. If He wills to make him will it without loving it—indeed, while disliking it, so that he does it despite his aversion—He makes him so.

This is not like one created being coercing another. A created being cannot produce in another’s heart either will and love or aversion and hatred. Rather, the most he can do is something that serves as

---

## Page 4217

a cause of desire or fear in him. When he coerces another person, he subjects him to punishment or threats that cause him apprehension and fear. The person then does what he would not choose to do and is not pleased to do. His aim is to ward off harm from himself. Thus, he wills the act, but his purpose is to avert harm, not the act itself. Accordingly, he may be described as choosing in one respect and not choosing in another, and as willing in one respect and not willing in another. In Arabic usage, however, he is not described as acting by choice, but as being coerced. This is also the usage of the jurists.

As is established in the two Sahīh collections, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When any of you supplicates, he should not say, ‘O Allah, forgive me if You will; O Allah, have mercy on me if You will.’ Rather, let him be firm in his request, for no one can compel Allah.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus explained that someone who acts by his own will is not coerced, whereas someone who is coerced acts by the will of another—the person coercing him. Although he intends what he does, and is not like someone who is merely acted upon and has no power or will whatsoever in the act, his primary purpose is to ward off the harm, not to perform the act itself. There are therefore three categories:

(The first is someone who is acted upon without having any ability to resist, such as a person who is carried against his will and taken into a place, or whose body is used to strike someone else, or a woman who is laid down and raped against her will, without any ability to resist. Such a person performs no voluntary act and has neither power nor will in the matter. An act of this kind is subject to neither command nor prohibition and incurs no punishment, by the agreement of all rational people. A person is punished only when able to resist but failing to do so, for if he does not

---

## Page 4218

resist, he is consenting rather than coerced. Hence the distinction between a woman who willingly engages in unlawful sexual intercourse and one who is forced into it.

The second category is someone who is coerced through beating, imprisonment, or the like until he acts. Such an act remains subject to religious responsibility, since he can refrain from it, even if he is killed as a result. Hence the jurists state that someone coerced into killing a person whose life is protected may not lawfully kill him. If he does kill him, however, they differ over retaliatory execution.

Most of them—including Mālik, Ahmad, and al-Shāfiʿī in one of his two opinions—hold that both the coerced person and the coercer are liable to retaliatory execution, because both participate in the killing. Abū Hanīfah holds that the wrongful coercer is liable, since the coerced person has become like an instrument. Zufar, however, holds that the coerced person who directly commits the killing is liable, because he is the direct perpetrator, whereas the other brings it about indirectly. He argues: “Had he been merely an instrument, he would not have been sinful, yet they agree that he is sinful.” Abū Yūsuf holds that neither is liable to retaliatory execution.

If, however, someone is coerced into drinking wine or performing similar acts, most of them permit him to do so. This is the position of Abū Hanīfah and al-Shāfiʿī, and the well-known position reported from Ahmad, on the basis of the words of Allah Most High:

“Do not force your slave girls into prostitution, if they wish to remain chaste, seeking the fleeting gains of this worldly life. And if anyone forces them, then after their being forced, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.”

As for a man who is coerced into unlawful sexual intercourse, there are two opinions within the school of Ahmad and among others. The first is that he is not considered to have been coerced into it. This is the opinion of Abū Hanīfah and Ahmad’s explicitly stated position.

---

## Page 4219

The second is that he may be coerced into it, as held by al-Shāfiʿī and a group of Ahmad’s followers. If someone is coerced into uttering words of disbelief, he may utter them while his heart remains secure in faith.

If someone is coerced into “legal transactions,” such as sale, marriage, divorce, zihār (declaring one’s wife forbidden by likening her to a woman one may not marry), īlā’ (swearing to abstain from marital intercourse), manumission, and the like, the majority—including Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and Ahmad—hold that any utterance he is wrongfully coerced into making is invalid. Thus, no divorce or manumission takes effect thereby, nor is he bound by any vow, oath, or other such undertaking. Abū Hanīfah, however, distinguishes between transactions which, in his view, admit of rescission and allow an option to cancel, such as sale and the like, and those which do not, such as marriage, divorce, and manumission. The former are not binding under coercion, whereas the latter are. As for someone who is rightfully coerced, such as a belligerent non-Muslim compelled to embrace Islam, what he is coerced into is binding upon him by agreement of the scholars.

Thus, the poet’s statement:

“If compulsion holds true, he is coerced;
And, in your view, the coerced is excused.”

is composed of two false premises.

## Page 4220

the first being: “If compulsion holds true, he is coerced.” It has already been established that if “compulsion” means compulsion in its familiar sense—one person forcing another to do what he does not want—then such compulsion is not established. If, however, it means that Allah creates a person’s will, then even if this compulsion is established, the person is not coerced.

The second premise is his statement: “In your view, the coerced is excused.” This is not so. Rather, those subjected to coercion fall into two categories. One consists of those who are rightfully coerced; they are not excused. Allah Most High never coerces anyone except rightfully, whether coercion is considered in terms of His creation and decree or His law and command. The only coerced person who is excused is someone wronged by being coerced without right. Allah Most High does not wrong anyone even by an atom’s weight. Rather, He is the Judge, the Just, who upholds justice, as He Most High says:

“Allah bears witness that there is no deity but Him, as do the angels and those endowed with knowledge; He upholds justice. There is no deity but Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise.”

Muslims and others agree that Allah is far removed from injustice. People have disagreed, however, over the meaning of the “injustice” from which the Lord must be declared free. The Qadariyyah, among the Muʿtazilah and others, regarded the “injustice” from which the Creator is declared free as being of the same kind as the “injustice” forbidden to created beings. They likened Allah Most High to His creation and thus imposed upon Him obligations of the same kind as those incumbent upon

created beings, and spoke contradictorily about justice and permissibility, as is well known of them. They also sought to bind others to numerous conclusions.

They said: “He has forbidden them to do that and offered them the prospect of reward if they obey Him and punishment if they disobey Him. They have committed injustice by their own choice, and preventing them would only have been possible by compelling them to desist. Such compulsion removes the moral accountability through which He offered them the prospect of reward.”

The majority replied to them:

“If one of us did this while knowing that his slaves would neither obey his command nor refrain from injustice, but would instead become increasingly disobedient and unjust, that would be neither wise nor just. Such conduct on the part of one of us is praiseworthy only because he does not know the outcome or is unable to prevent the wrongdoing. Allah, however, knows all outcomes and has power over all things. Otherwise, if one of us knew that, were he to command them in order to offer them the prospect of reward, they would disobey him and wrong one another, he would be obliged to compel them to desist from injustice.”

A full discussion of this matter is set out elsewhere, for this reply allows only a brief indication.

it is dipped into the sea. O My servants, these are but your deeds: I record them for you and then recompense you for them in full. Whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame no one but himself.”

At the beginning of this hadith related from Allah—which Imām Ahmad described as “the noblest hadith transmitted by the people of Syria”—He states that He has forbidden injustice for Himself. “Prohibition” is the opposite of imposing an obligation. Thus, the Exalted says:

Whoever says it in the evening with firm conviction in it and dies that night will enter Paradise.”

## Page 4226

This hadith includes the words:

“I acknowledge Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin.”

Among His blessings upon His believing servant are the faith and good deeds He enables him to attain. These come from His grace, kindness, mercy and wisdom, while the servant’s evil deeds fall within His justice and wisdom. Every blessing from Him is an act of grace, and every punishment from Him is an act of justice. He is not questioned about what He does because of the perfection of His wisdom, mercy and justice—not merely because of His overwhelming might and power, as Jahm and his followers maintain.

This has been discussed at length, and the true meaning of the following words has been explained:

“All good is in Your hands, and evil is not attributable to You.”

This is so even though He is the Creator of all things. It has also been explained that evil is ascribed to Allah in the Quran and Sunnah only in one of three ways:

First, within a general statement, such as:

“Allah is the Creator of all things.”

Second, by ascribing it to its cause, as in His words:

“From the evil of what He has created.”

Third, by leaving its agent unmentioned, as in the words of the jinn:

“We do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends guidance for them.”

He brings together “the three categories” in al-Fātihah, saying:

“All praise is for Allah, Lord of all worlds.”

This is a general statement. He also says:

“The path of those You have blessed, not of those who have incurred wrath.”

Here He leaves the agent of wrath unmentioned. Then He says:

“Nor of those who have gone astray.”

Thus, He ascribes going astray to the created being. Another example is the statement of Allah’s intimate friend:

“And when I am ill, it is He who heals me.”

---

## Page 4227

and the words of al-Khidr:

“So I intended to damage it.”

“So we intended that their Lord should replace him for them with one better in purity and closer in affection.”

“So your Lord intended that they should reach maturity.”

The true nature of these matters has been discussed at length, and it has been explained that Allah has created nothing without a wise purpose. The Most High says:

“Who perfected everything He created.”

And He says:

“The work of Allah, who has perfected all things.”

Thus, a created thing is good and reflects wisdom when considered in relation to the wise purpose for which it was created. Even if it involves evil in another respect, that evil is incidental and limited in scope; it is not pure evil. Rather, evil intended to bring about a greater good is good on the part of the wise agent, even though it is evil for the one affected by it.

Anyone who supposes that the intended wise purpose could be fully realized without that evil does so only because he lacks knowledge of the true nature of things and their interconnectedness. For when the Creator creates something, He must also create what its existence necessarily entails: a thing cannot exist without its necessary concomitants. He must also refrain from creating its incompatible opposites, for two mutually exclusive opposites cannot coexist at the same time.

He—glorified be He—has power over all things; nothing is excluded from this universal statement. However, the term “thing” denotes that whose existence is conceivable. What is intrinsically impossible is not a thing, as all people of reason agree.

---

## Page 4228

And the power to create opposites is the power to create either one as an alternative to the other. Thus, if He—glorified be He—wills to make a servant move, He does so; and if He wills to make him remain still, He does so. The same applies to faith and disbelief, and to other opposites. It is inconceivable, however, for a servant to possess mutually opposed attributes at the same time: to be a truthful believer among Allah’s pious friends and also a disbeliever and hypocrite among Allah’s enemies. Nevertheless, a branch of faith and a branch of hypocrisy may coexist within him.

The servant must know that Allah’s knowledge, power, wisdom, and mercy are supremely perfect, such that no greater perfection is conceivable. Indeed, every possible perfection free of deficiency necessarily belongs to the Lord Most High. Some servants may know something of His wisdom, while other aspects remain hidden from them. People differ in their knowledge of His wisdom, mercy, and justice.

The more a servant knows the true nature of things, the more he knows of Allah’s wisdom, justice, mercy, and power. He comes to know that Allah bestows upon him the blessing of good deeds—both their performance and their reward—and that whatever punishment he suffers for his sins is through the justice of Allah Most High. He also knows that his very commission of sins—although it falls within what the Lord has decreed—is due to his soul’s inherent deficiency, incapacity, and ignorance; and that whatever goodness is within his soul comes from Allah’s action, kindness, and generosity. He further knows that, although the Lord created the soul, fashioned it, and inspired it with its wickedness and its piety, this inspiration of wickedness and piety took place

---

## Page 4229

with consummate wisdom: were all people of reason, from the first generations to the last, to come together to conceive of any greater wisdom, they could not do so. Yet many people cannot grasp the details of the Lord’s wisdom, and some aspects of it are beyond the knowledge of all creation, even the angels.

Thus, when Allah Most High said to the angels, “I will place a successor on earth,” they said, “Will You place in it someone who will spread corruption there and shed blood?” He said:

“Indeed, I know what you do not know.”

A general understanding and an overall faith therefore suffice for them. Allah—glorified be He—has commanded them to ask Him for everything they need: guidance, right judgment, well-being in this life and the Hereafter, forgiveness, and mercy.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say, as reported in an authentic hadith:

“O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity, and self-sufficiency.”

He would also say:

“O Allah, grant my soul its piety and purify it; You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and Master.”

And he would say:

“O Allah, set right for me my religion, which safeguards all my affairs; set right for me my worldly life, in which I make my living; and set right for me my Hereafter, to which I shall return. Make life an increase for me in every good, and make death a relief for me from every evil.”

All of these supplications occur in hadiths recorded in the Sahīh.

Sahīh Muslim also reports that, when he rose at night, he would say:

“O Allah, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Isrāfīl, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You

---

## Page 4230

judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differed. Guide me, by Your leave, to the truth concerning which they have differed. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path.”

Allah Most High has commanded us to say in our prayers:

“Guide us to the straight path—the path of those You have blessed, not of those who have incurred Your anger, nor of those who have gone astray.”

This is the finest of supplications and the most binding upon His servants. Whoever truly embraces this supplication, Allah will make him one of those who are guided and rightly directed. Indeed, He hears supplication and never breaks His promise. And Allah knows best.

## Page 4231

He was asked about someone who had been killed:
“Did he die at his appointed time, or did the killer cut his appointed term short?”

The Answer

He replied:

Someone who is killed is like anyone else who dies: no one dies before his appointed time, nor does anyone live beyond it. Indeed, all animals and trees have appointed terms that neither come early nor are delayed. A thing’s appointed term is the end of its lifespan, while its lifespan is the duration of its existence. Thus, the lifespan is the duration of existence, and the appointed term is the point at which that lifespan expires.

It is established in Sahīh Muslim and elsewhere that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah decreed the destinies of His creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and His Throne was over the water.”

It is also established in Sahīh al-Bukhārī that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah existed, and nothing existed before Him. His Throne was over the water, and He wrote everything in the Record and created the heavens and the earth.”

In another wording: “Then He created the heavens and the earth.”

Allah Most High has said:

“When their appointed time comes, they cannot delay it for a moment, nor can they bring it forward.”

Allah knows what will happen before it happens, and He has written it down. Thus, He knows that this person will die

---

## Page 4232

from an abdominal illness, pleurisy, a collapsing building, drowning, or some other cause, while another will be killed—whether by poison, the sword, a stone, or some other means of killing. Allah’s knowledge of this and His recording of it—indeed, His willing and creating all things—do not preclude praise and blame, reward and punishment.

Rather, if someone carries out a killing commanded by Allah and His Messenger—as does one fighting in Allah’s cause—Allah rewards him for it. If he carries out a killing forbidden by Allah and His Messenger—as highway robbers and aggressors do—Allah punishes him for it. If he carries out a permissible killing, such as someone exacting legal retribution, he is neither rewarded nor punished, unless a good or evil intention earns him one or the other.

Appointed terms are of two kinds: an “unconditional appointed term,” known to Allah, and a “conditional appointed term.” This clarifies the meaning of the Prophet’s saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Whoever would like his provision to be increased and his lifespan extended, let him maintain his ties of kinship.”

For Allah has commanded the angel to record an appointed term for him and has said: “If he maintains his ties of kinship, I shall add such and such to it.” The angel does not know whether it will be increased, but Allah knows what the final outcome will be. When that appointed time comes, it can neither be brought forward nor delayed.

Had the slain person not been killed, some of the Qadariyyah have said that he would have lived, while some who deny causation have said that he would have died. Both views are mistaken. For Allah knew that he would die by being killed. Thus, supposing the contrary of what He knows means considering how something that will not happen would unfold if it did happen. People may or may not know the answer to this. Thus, if we were to suppose that Allah knew he would not be killed, it would be possible that

---

## Page 4233

He had decreed his death at this time, and it would also be possible that He had decreed that he live until another time. To assert either possibility with certainty under a supposition that will never be realized is ignorance.

This is like someone asking: “Had this person not eaten the provision decreed for him, would he have died or been provided with something else?” Or someone asking: “Had this man not made this woman pregnant, would she have remained barren, or would another man have made her pregnant? Had this land not been cultivated, would someone else have cultivated it, or would it have remained wasteland where nothing was grown? As for this person who learned the Quran from this teacher, had the teacher not taught him, would he have learned from someone else, or would he never have learned the Quran at all?” There are many such examples.

## Page 4234

Shaykh al-Islām was asked:

“Are high and low prices from Allah Most High, or not?”

He replied:

Everything besides Allah—entities, their attributes, and their states—is created by Allah and belongs to Him. He is their Lord, Creator, Sovereign, and the One who governs their affairs. They have no Lord other than Him, and there is no god besides Him. To Him belong creation and command; He has neither partner nor helper in any of this. Rather, as He, glorified be He, says:

“Say, ‘Call upon those whom you claim to be gods besides Allah.’ They do not possess an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have any share in either, nor does He have any helper among them.”

“Intercession does not benefit with Him except for those to whom He gives permission.”

He, glorified be He, has stated that those invoked besides Him possess not even an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth, have no share in ownership, and provide no assistance in anything.

These are the three grounds upon which another party’s right is established: someone either owns a thing outright, is an equal partner in its ownership, or is neither of these but assists its owner—as a minister, adviser, teacher, rescuer, or supporter does. He, glorified be He, has thus made clear that no one besides Him owns even an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor does anyone besides Him have any share in that, whether small or great. Thus, they do not

---

## Page 4235

own anything, nor do they have a share in anything. Nor does He, glorified be He, have any helper—that is, anyone who supports or assists Him. He has no minister, adviser, or helper. This accords with His words, glorified be He:

“And say, ‘Praise be to Allah, who has never taken a son, nor has He any partner in His dominion, nor does He need a protector out of weakness.’ And proclaim His greatness.”

A creature takes another creature as an ally because of his own weakness; when he has an ally to support him, he gains strength through that ally. But the Lord Most High does not take anyone as an ally because of any weakness on His part—exalted is He. Rather, He is mighty in Himself:

“Whoever desires might, all might belongs to Allah.”

He takes His believing servants as allies only out of His mercy, grace, wisdom, kindness, generosity, bounty, and beneficence.

Accordingly, high and low prices—resulting from prices rising and falling—are among the events that have no creator but Allah alone. None of them occurs except by His will and power. Yet He, glorified be He, has made some human actions causes of certain events, just as He has made a killer’s act of killing a cause of the victim’s death. He has also made people’s wrongdoing a possible cause of rising prices, and some people’s benevolence a possible cause of falling prices.

For this reason, some Qadarī Mu‘tazilites and others have attributed high and low prices to certain people, and have built unsound principles upon this:

(First: that human actions are not created by Allah Most High.

---

## Page 4236

And second: that whatever a person’s action causes is brought into being by that person.

And (third: that high and low prices arise only through this cause. These principles are false. It has been established that Allah is the Creator of everything, including human actions and all else. Abundant scriptural and rational evidence demonstrates this, and the early generations of this Ummah and its leading scholars agree upon it.

At the same time, they maintain that people possess power and will, and that they perform their own actions. They also affirm the causes Allah has created and the wisdom embodied in His creation.

The question of divine decree is a momentous one concerning which two groups have gone astray. One group denied that Allah is the Creator of everything and that whatever He wills occurs, while whatever He does not will does not occur. Such was the denial of the Muʿtazilites.

Another group denied that people perform their own actions, that they possess power which actually affects what lies within its scope, that anything created can be a cause of something else, or that Allah created anything for a wise purpose. Such was the denial of Jahm ibn Safwān and those who followed him among the proponents of compulsion, many of whom have been associated with the Sunnah. This question is discussed at length elsewhere.

As for the second principle—namely, that for which a person’s action is one of the causes, such as satiety

---

## Page 4237

that results from eating, and the loss of life that results from killing—most Muʿtazilites regard such effects as actions performed by the person. The proponents of compulsion, however, attribute no causal influence to the person’s action. Even where they are certain that something is a cause, they say: “The effect occurs when it occurs, not through it.” As for the early generations and the leading scholars, they do not regard a person as producing such effects in the same way that he performs his own bodily movements. They do not, however, rule out his contributing to their causes, or Allah’s having made his action, together with other factors, causes that bring about such effects.

Allah mentions both kinds in His Book, saying:

“This is because no thirst, fatigue, or hunger afflicts them in the cause of Allah, nor do they tread any ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor inflict any loss upon an enemy, without a righteous deed being recorded for them thereby. Indeed, Allah does not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.”

“Nor do they spend anything, small or great, or cross any valley, without it being recorded for them, so that Allah may reward them according to the best of what they used to do.”

Spending and travelling are their own actions, performed by them. Thus, concerning these He said, “without it being recorded for them,” rather than “without a righteous deed being recorded for them thereby.” These things are themselves deeds, so merely recording them fulfils the intended purpose. This is unlike thirst, fatigue, and hunger arising apart from jihad, and unlike the disbelievers’ rage at the losses inflicted upon them. These are not the people’s own actions; rather, they arise from causes that include their actions. Hence the Most High said:

“Without a righteous deed being recorded for them thereby.”

It is therefore clear that the effects arising from people’s actions count as deeds for them, because their actions were a cause of those effects. As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever calls others to guidance will receive, by way of

---

## Page 4238

reward, the equivalent of the rewards of those who follow him, without their rewards being diminished in any way. Whoever calls others to misguidance will bear a burden of sin equivalent to the sins of those who follow him, without their sins being diminished in any way.”

And (the third principle:

High and low prices do not arise solely from wrongdoing on the part of some people. They may also result from a scarcity of the desired goods being created or brought in. When demand for something increases while its supply decreases, its price rises; when its supply increases while demand decreases, its price falls. Scarcity and abundance may arise without any human involvement, or from a cause involving no wrongdoing, or from a cause involving wrongdoing. Allah Most High instils desires in people’s hearts.

Thus it is He—glory be to Him—as mentioned in the report:

“Prices may be high while desires are meagre, and prices may be low while desires are impoverished.”

## Page 4239

Shaykh al-Islām Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah sanctify his soul—was asked about what Abū Hāmid al-Ghazālī said in his book known as Minhāj al-‘Ābidīn (The Path of Worshippers), concerning provisions for the Hereafter, under the fourth obstacle, namely impediments. Following an earlier discussion of reliance upon Allah in which he stated that provision is guaranteed, he said:

“If it is asked, ‘Is the servant obliged under any circumstances to seek provision?’ know that the guaranteed provision is nourishment and the sustaining of life. It cannot, therefore, be sought, since it is something Allah brings about in the servant, like life and death: the servant cannot bring it about or ward it off. As for the allotted means of provision, the servant is not obliged to seek them, for he has no need of them. His need is only for what is guaranteed, which comes from Allah and is guaranteed by Him.

“As for His saying, Most High,

‘And seek Allah’s bounty,’

what is meant is knowledge and reward. It has also been said that this is instead a permission: since it is a command issued after a prohibition, it indicates permissibility, not obligation or compulsion.

“If it is asked, ‘But this guaranteed provision has means through which it comes about; are we obliged to seek those means?’ the reply is: You are not obliged to seek them, for the servant has no need of them, since Allah—glory be to Him—brings it about

---

## Page 4240

through means or without them. On what grounds, then, are we obliged to seek those means? Moreover, Allah has given an unconditional guarantee, without making it dependent upon seeking or earning. He, Most High, says:

‘There is no creature on earth but that Allah provides for it.’

How, then, could He command the servant to seek something when he does not know where to look for it? For he does not know through which of these means he will obtain his provision (nor does he know which has been made the particular means of his nourishment and sustenance). None of us knows precisely what that means is or where it has come from. It is therefore not valid to impose this obligation upon him. Reflect upon this—may you be rightly guided—for it is clear. Furthermore, it suffices that the prophets—Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them—and the righteous servants who relied upon Allah did not, for the most part, seek provision, but devoted themselves entirely to worship. There is consensus that, in doing so, they were neither neglecting Allah’s command nor disobeying Him. Thus, you cannot regard seeking provision and its means as something the servant is commanded to do as a binding obligation.”

What, then, is the distinction between this imam’s statement and what is explicitly stated in the works of the imams, including works of jurisprudence and others: namely, that the servant must seek provision and pursue its means? Indeed, they go further: if the servant needs provision and finds that someone else has more than he needs, he must ask him for it. If that person refuses, he must compel him, even if that means killing him. Does what is explicitly stated in al-Minhāj apply to some people but not others? Please clarify the apparent contradiction between these two statements that has perplexed us—may you be rewarded—and explain the matter fully.

He replied—may Allah be pleased with him:

---

## Page 4241

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. A group of people have adopted this view expressed by Abū Hāmid. However, the imams of the Muslims and the majority of Muslims hold the contrary view: earning a livelihood may be obligatory, recommended, disliked, permissible, or forbidden. It is therefore impermissible to state categorically that none of it is obligatory, just as it is impermissible to state categorically that none of it is forbidden. The means that the servant is commanded to pursue, whether as an obligation or a recommendation, consist in worshipping Allah and obeying Him and His Messenger. Allah has obliged His servants to worship Him and rely upon Him.

As He, Most High, says:

“So worship Him and rely upon Him.”

And He says:

“Remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself wholeheartedly to Him.”

“Lord of the east and the west; there is no god but Him, so take Him as your Guardian.”

And He says:

“Whoever fears Allah, He will make a way out for him.”

“And provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him.”

Fearing Allah encompasses doing what Allah has commanded and refraining from what He has forbidden.

It is related from Abū Dharr that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“O Abū Dharr, if all people acted upon this verse, it would suffice them.”

For this reason, one of the early generations said, “No God-fearing person has ever been in need.” He meant that Allah has guaranteed those who fear Him a way out of the difficulties that beset people, and provision from where they do not expect. Thus, He wards off what harms them and brings them what they need.

If this does not happen, it indicates a deficiency in one’s fear of Allah; one should therefore seek Allah’s forgiveness and repent to Him. Hence, in the hadith traced back to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and narrated by al-Tirmidhī, he said:

“Whoever

---

## Page 4242

frequently seeks Allah’s forgiveness, Allah will grant him relief from every worry, a way out of every difficulty, and provision from where he does not expect.”

The point is that Allah has not commanded reliance upon Him alone. Alongside reliance, He has commanded worship of Him and fear of Him, which entails doing what He has commanded and refraining from what He has warned against. Whoever thinks that he can please his Lord by relying upon Him without doing what he has been commanded is misguided, just as whoever thinks he can do what earns Allah’s pleasure without relying upon Him is misguided. Rather, performing the worship that Allah has commanded is obligatory.

When the term “worship” is used without qualification, it includes reliance upon Allah. When the two are mentioned together, reliance has its own distinct designation. The same applies to comparable expressions, such as fearing Allah and obeying the Messenger: when “fearing Allah” is used without qualification, it includes obeying the Messenger. Yet one may also be conjoined with the other, as in the words of Noah, peace be upon him:

“Worship Allah.”

Likewise, Allah says:

“Fear Allah and speak upright words.”

There are other similar examples.

Allah has coupled worship of Him with reliance upon Him in several places, as in His words, Most High:

“Say: He is my Lord; there is no god but Him. In Him I put my trust, and to Him is my return.”

And in the words of Shuʿayb:

“In Him I put my trust, and to Him I turn.”

For turning to Allah and returning to Him in repentance mean returning to Him through worshipping Him, obeying Him, and obeying His Messenger. A servant cannot be obedient to Allah and His Messenger—let alone be among His chosen, God-fearing allies—unless he does what He has commanded and refrains from what He has forbidden. Reliance upon Allah is included in this.

---

## Page 4243

As for whoever thinks that reliance upon Allah dispenses with the means He has commanded, he is misguided. This is like someone who thinks he can rely on the felicity or misery decreed for him without doing what Allah has commanded. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about this very question. As reported in both Sahīh collections, he said:

“There is not one of you whose place in Paradise or Hell has not already been written.” He was asked, “O Messenger of Allah, should we not then abandon deeds and rely on what has been written?” He replied, “No. Act, for everyone will be enabled to do that for which he was created.”

Likewise, both Sahīh collections report that he was asked:

“Tell us about the deeds people perform and strive to accomplish: do they concern matters for which the pens have already dried and the scrolls have been rolled up?”

When he was asked, “Should we not then rely on what has been written?” he replied, “No. Act, for everyone will be enabled to do that for which he was created.”

He, peace and blessings be upon him, also explained that the means Allah has created and prescribed are themselves part of the divine decree. He was asked:

“Tell us about the healing recitations we seek, the protective measures we take, and the medicines we use: do they avert anything of Allah’s decree?” He replied, “They are part of Allah’s decree.”

Placing one’s trust in means is to associate partners with Allah, violating His oneness; denying that means have any causal role is a deficiency in reason; and turning away from the means Allah has commanded undermines the revealed law. A servant’s heart must therefore rely upon Allah, not upon any means. Allah will make available to him the means that benefit him in this world and the Hereafter. If the means are

---

## Page 4244

within his power and he is commanded to pursue them, he should do so while relying upon Allah, just as he performs his obligatory duties, fights the enemy, carries weapons, and wears armour. He does not rely on trust alone to repel the enemy without undertaking the fighting he has been commanded to undertake. Whoever abandons the prescribed means is ineffectual, negligent, and blameworthy.

In Sahīh Muslim, Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, reports that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is good in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek Allah’s help, and do not give up. If something befalls you, do not say, ‘If only I had done such-and-such, such-and-such would have happened.’ Rather, say, ‘Allah has decreed it, and He has done what He willed,’ for ‘if only’ opens the door to Satan’s work.”

Sunan Abī Dāwūd reports:

“Two men brought their dispute before the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he ruled against one of them. The man against whom he ruled said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.’ He, peace and blessings be upon him, said, ‘Allah censures inaction. Rather, you must act prudently; then, if something overcomes you, say, “Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.”’”

People have discussed carrying provisions on Hajj and other journeys. The established practice of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, his rightly guided caliphs, his Companions, those who followed them in righteousness, and the foremost religious masters is to carry provisions. Doing so entails obedience to Allah and His Messenger, benefits the person carrying them, and enables him to benefit others. A “group” has claimed that perfect reliance upon Allah requires not carrying provisions. Yet this view has been rejected by

---

## Page 4245

the leading scholars. Al-Hārith al-Muhāsibī, for example, refuted it in his Book of Reliance upon Allah, attributing this view to Shaqīq al-Balkhī. He vigorously refuted those who held it, presenting arguments that demonstrated their error: they misunderstood the true nature of reliance upon Allah and were disobeying Allah by neglecting acts of obedience to Him.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal was told about one of the extremists who were ignorant of the true nature of reliance upon Allah: when food was set before him, he would not reach for it, waiting for it to be put into his mouth. When it was offered, he would keep his mouth shut until others opened it and put the food inside. Ahmad condemned this in the strongest terms. Some of these people declared earning a living unlawful.

This and similar errors arise from insufficient knowledge of Allah’s way in His creation and His commands. Allah created things through causes and prescribed for His servants means by which they attain His forgiveness, mercy, and reward in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever supposes that reliance upon Allah alone will secure what he seeks, while he neglects the means Allah has commanded him to pursue, and that desired outcomes do not depend upon the means Allah has appointed for them, is mistaken.

Although Allah, glorified be He, has guaranteed His servant’s provision and will certainly provide for him throughout his life, this does not preclude that guaranteed provision from having means that involve the servant’s own actions or occur independently of them.

Moreover, He may provide for him through lawful or unlawful means. If the servant does what Allah has commanded him to do, He provides for him through lawful means; if he neglects what Allah has commanded him to do, He may provide for him through unlawful means.

Supplication and reliance upon Allah fall into this same category. Some people have supposed that these have no effect

---

## Page 4246

in attaining what is sought or averting what is feared, but are purely acts of worship, and that whatever is attained through them would have been attained without them. Others have supposed that they are merely a sign. The correct view, held by the early generations, the leading scholars, and the majority, is that they are among the greatest means of attaining happiness in this world and the Hereafter.

Regarding what Allah has decreed through supplication, reliance upon Him, earning a living, and other means, asking, “What would happen if the means were absent?” is like asking, “Would this slain person have lived had he not been killed?” Some of the Qadarīs have supposed that he would have lived, while some who affiliate themselves with the Sunnah have supposed that he would have died. The correct view is that this is a decree concerning something Allah knew would occur: Allah decreed his death through this cause, so he would die only through it. Likewise, Allah decreed a person’s happiness in this world and the Hereafter through his worship, supplication, reliance upon Him, righteous deeds, and earning a living; it is attained only through these means. If one supposes this cause to be absent, one does not know what would have been decreed. On that supposition, it might have been decreed that he would die, or it might have been decreed that he would live. To assert either with certainty is mistaken.

If someone were to say, “I will neither eat nor drink. If Allah has decreed that I should live, He will keep me alive without food or drink,” he would be a fool, like someone who says, “I will not have intercourse with my wife. If Allah has decreed a child for me, she will conceive without a man.”

## Page 4247

Section

With this understood, some of those who follow the path to Allah are unable to earn a living while fulfilling what Allah has commanded them of jihad, learning, worship, and other duties. They include those whom Allah mentions in His words:

“For the poor who are restricted in Allah’s cause and cannot travel through the land. Those unaware of their circumstances think them wealthy because they refrain from asking. You will recognize them by their appearance; they do not ask people insistently.”

They also include those whom Allah mentions in His words:

“For the poor Emigrants who were driven from their homes and their property, seeking Allah’s bounty and pleasure and supporting Allah and His Messenger. They are the truthful.”

The first group are recipients of charity, while the second are recipients of fay’. Concerning the first group, Allah Most High says:

“If you give charity openly, that is good; but if you conceal it and give it to the poor, that is better for you, and He will expiate some of your sins. Allah is fully aware of what you do.”

The passage continues to His words:

“For the poor who are restricted in Allah’s cause.”

Concerning the “second group,” He says:

“Whatever Allah has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah, the Messenger, his close relatives, orphans, the needy, and the traveller.”

The passage continues to His words:

“For the poor Emigrants.”

Then He says:

“And those who had already settled in the city and embraced the faith before them.”

Thus, He mentioned the Emigrants and the Helpers. The Emigrants were predominantly

---

## Page 4248

engaged in trade, while the Helpers were predominantly engaged in agriculture. He said to both groups:

“Spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have brought forth for you from the earth.”

He thus mentioned zakat on trade and zakat on what comes out of the earth, which is one-tenth, half a tenth, or a quarter of a tenth.

Some of those who follow the path to Allah can earn a living while fulfilling those duties. When Allah Most High commanded them to pray at night, He said:

“He knows that some of you will be ill, others travelling through the land seeking Allah’s bounty, and others fighting in Allah’s cause.”

He thus divided the Muslims into four groups: those devoted to the Quran, knowledge, and worship; those travelling through the land seeking Allah’s bounty; those striving in Allah’s cause; and, fourth, those who are excused.

As for the claim, “Nourishment and sustenance are acts of Allah and therefore cannot be sought, just like life,” this is not so. Rather, whatever Allah brings about through causes can be sought by pursuing those causes. The same applies to life and death: death can be sought or averted through the causes Allah has decreed. If we wish an enemy of Allah to die, we seek to kill him; and if we wish to avert death from the believers, we avert it through the means Allah has prescribed. Allah Most High said concerning David, peace be upon him:

“We taught him the craft of making armour for you to protect you in battle.”

And Allah Most High said:

“Garments that protect you from the heat, and garments that protect you in battle.”

And Allah Most High said:

“Let them pray with you, taking their precautions and carrying their weapons.”

Likewise, shielding us from heat and cold is an act of Allah—hence clothing and earning a living—just as warding off hunger and thirst is an act of Allah through food and drink.

---

## Page 4249

and this is just as taking life is an act of Allah, yet one may seek to bring it about by killing. Likewise, knowledge and guidance arising in the heart are acts of Allah, yet one may seek them through their prescribed means and through supplication.

As for someone saying, “Allah acts both with and without a cause, so why must we pursue the means?” the answer is:

That is not so. Rather, everything Allah creates and decrees, He creates and decrees through causes. Some causes, however, lie beyond a person’s power, while others are within it; some are brought about by the person, while others are not. Some causes are “customary,” while others are “rare.” In some years, He may withhold rain and nourish the crops with a wind He sends. Likewise, food and drink may be multiplied through the supplication of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or of a righteous man; this too is one of the causes.

Undoubtedly, provision may come through created beings. Some people have their provision brought to them by a jinn, an angel, or certain birds or beasts. This is rare, however; most people receive their provision through other human beings. For example, most of those unable to pursue the means of earning a living receive their provision through people who give to them, whether as charity, gifts, offerings in fulfilment of vows, or anything else Allah grants them through those whom He makes available to them.

## Page 4250

It is authentically reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Son of Adam, spending your surplus is better for you, while withholding it is worse for you. There is no blame in retaining enough to meet your needs. The upper hand is better than the lower hand.”

Another authentic hadith states:

“Allah’s hand is the highest; the giver’s hand comes next, and the beggar’s hand is the lowest.”

Some people claim that the hand of the beggar who receives is the upper hand, because charity falls into the hand of the True One. This contradicts the explicit statement of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that Allah’s hand is the highest, the giver’s hand comes next, and the beggar’s hand is the lowest.

As for someone saying, “Allah has given an unconditional guarantee,” the response is: This does not negate the obligation to pursue the means as required. What He has guaranteed includes the provision of children, animals, and wives. Nevertheless, by the consensus of the Muslims, a man must provide for his children, his animals, and his wife. Providing for himself is an even greater obligation upon him.

As for someone asking, “How can a person seek something when he does not know where it is?” the answer is: He pursues the means he has been commanded to pursue and relies upon Allah concerning what lies beyond his ability. He is like someone who ploughs the earth and sows the seed, then relies upon Allah to send down rain, make the crops grow, and ward off harmful things. Likewise, the merchant’s ability extends only to obtaining merchandise and transporting it. But as for desire for it being instilled in a prospective buyer’s heart and his paying a price that yields a profit, this

---

## Page 4251

is beyond a person’s power. Whoever does what he is capable of will not be punished by Allah for what he is unable to do. Nor is the pursuit directed towards any particular thing, but rather towards sufficient provision—just as someone supplicates to Allah for provision and enough to meet his needs, without specifying anything in particular.

Section

Once this is understood, earning a living is obligatory in some circumstances. For example, a man may need to provide for himself or his dependants, or repay his debt, while being capable of earning and not occupied with something Allah has commanded that is more virtuous in His sight than earning a living. Such a person is obliged to earn a living, by scholarly consensus. If he neglects to do so, he is disobedient and sinful.

In other circumstances, earning is recommended, as when such a person earns something to give in charity. It is authentically reported in the two Sahīh collections, on the authority of Abū Mūsā, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Charity is due from every Muslim.”

They asked, “Messenger of Allah, what if he has nothing?”

He replied, “He should work with his hands, benefiting himself and giving charity.”

They asked, “What if he cannot do that?”

He replied, “He should help someone in need who is distressed.”

They asked, “What if he cannot do that?”

He replied, “Then he should enjoin what is right and refrain from evil, for that counts as charity for him.”

## Page 4252

Section

As for the claim that the prophets and the friends of Allah did not seek provision, this is not so. Rather, most prophets pursued means by which they obtained their provision. Thus our Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in the hadith narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar:

“I was sent with the sword before the Hour, until Allah alone is worshipped, without any partner. My provision was placed beneath the shade of my spear, and humiliation and abasement were imposed upon those who oppose my command. Whoever imitates a people is one of them.”

It is also authentically reported in the Sahīh that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The best food a man eats is that which comes from his own earnings.”

David ate from his own earnings and used to make armour. Zechariah was a carpenter. Abraham, Allah’s close friend, owned so much livestock that he would serve a fattened calf to guests he did not know. Such hospitality is possible only with ample means.

The finest of Allah’s friends who relied upon Him were the Emigrants and the Helpers. Abū Bakr al-Siddīq was the foremost of Allah’s friends who relied upon Him after the prophets. Allah provided for most of them through means they pursued. Al-Siddīq was a merchant, and he would take his share of the spoils of war; and when he assumed

---

## Page 4253

the caliphate, he was allotted two dirhams a day from the public treasury. He had given away all his wealth, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked him:

“What have you left for your family?”

He replied: “I have left them Allah and His Messenger.”

Despite this, he would take nothing from anyone—neither charity, nor futūh (gifts), nor vowed offerings. Rather, he lived solely on his own earnings. This contrasts with someone who claims to rely upon Allah and gives away all his wealth, imagining that he is following al-Siddīq’s example, while accepting things from people, whether by asking or without asking. This was not the way of Abū Bakr al-Siddīq. Indeed, al-Musnad relates:

“When al-Siddīq dropped his whip, he would dismount and pick it up, rather than say to anyone, ‘Hand it to me.’ He would say, ‘My beloved instructed me not to ask people for anything.’”

How far removed this is from those who make begging and asking people a path to Allah, even instructing the spiritual aspirant to beg from others!

Hadiths transmitted from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, through numerous independent chains prohibit asking people except in cases of necessity. He said:

“Begging is not lawful except for someone burdened by an overwhelming debt, a grievous blood-money liability, or dire poverty.”

Allah Most High says:

“So when you have finished, strive hard.”

“And to your Lord direct your longing.”

Thus He commanded him to direct his longing to Allah alone. Some of these people regard supplicating Allah and asking of Him as a deficiency, yet they themselves ask people and persistently beg from them. For a servant to ask his Lord for what he needs is among the finest acts of worship, and it is the way of Allah’s prophets. He has commanded His servants to ask of Him, saying:

“And ask Allah of His bounty.”

And He praised

## Page 4254

those who call upon their Lord with hope and fear. Some supplications are obligatory upon every Muslim, such as the supplication contained in the opening chapter of the Quran.

Some of these people appeal to a report about Abraham, Allah’s close friend: when he was cast into the fire, Gabriel asked him:

“Do you need anything?”

He replied, “From you, no.”

Gabriel said, “Then ask.”

Abraham replied, “His knowledge of my condition suffices me without my asking.”

The beginning of this report—his words, “From you, no”—is well known. It is also authentically reported in Sahīh al-Bukhārī that Ibn ‘Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said concerning the words “Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs”:

“Abraham said these words when he was cast into the fire, and Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said them when people told him, ‘Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.’”

As for the words, “His knowledge of my condition suffices me without my asking,” this is a false statement. It contradicts what Allah has related about Abraham, His close friend, and the other prophets: their supplications to Allah and their requests of Him. It also contradicts Allah’s command that His servants ask Him for well-being in this world and the Hereafter, as in their words:

“Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.”

Supplicating Allah, asking of Him, and relying upon Him are acts of worship of Allah, prescribed in connection with means, just as He decrees outcomes through means. How, then, could His knowledge alone dispense with what He has created and commanded? Allah knows best. May Allah bless Muhammad and grant him peace.

## Page 4255

Shaykh al-Islām was asked about provision:

“Does it increase or decrease? Is it what a person eats or what he owns?”

He answered:

Provision is of two kinds:

The first is what Allah knows He will provide for a person. This does not change.

The second is what He has recorded and made known to the angels. This increases and decreases according to the means involved. Allah commands the angels to record a certain provision for a person; if he maintains his ties of kinship, Allah increases it beyond that amount. As recorded in the Sahīh, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever would be pleased to have his provision increased and his life prolonged should maintain his ties of kinship.”

Likewise, David’s lifespan was increased by sixty years: Allah made it one hundred years after it had been forty.

Another example of this is the supplication of ‘Umar:

“O Allah, if You have recorded me as wretched, erase that and record me as blessed, for You erase whatever You will and confirm whatever You will.”

Another example is what Allah Most High relates from Noah:

“Worship Allah, fear Him, and obey me.”

“He will forgive you some of your sins and grant you respite until an appointed term.”

There is abundant evidence for this. The means through which provision is obtained are themselves among the things Allah has decreed and recorded. If He has already decreed that He will provide for a person through his efforts and earnings, He inspires him to strive and earn.

---

## Page 4256

and what He has decreed for him through earning cannot be obtained without earning. Whatever He has decreed for him without earning—as when someone from whom he inherits dies—comes to him without earning. Striving is of two kinds:

Striving through established means of obtaining provision, such as craftsmanship, agriculture, and trade; and striving through supplication, reliance upon Allah, kindness to others, and similar deeds. For Allah helps His servant as long as the servant helps his brother.

Section

Provision has two meanings:

The first is what a person benefits from.

The second is what a person owns. This second meaning is intended in His words:

“and spend out of what We have provided for them”

and His words:

“And spend from what We have provided for you.”

This refers to the lawful property that Allah has granted him ownership of.

As for the first meaning, it is intended in His words:

“There is no creature on earth whose provision is not guaranteed by Allah”

and in the words of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“No soul will die until it has received its provision in full,”

and similar statements. A person may consume what is lawful or unlawful; it counts as provision in this first sense, but not in the second. Whatever he acquires but does not benefit from counts as provision in the second sense, not the first, for in reality it is his heir’s wealth, not his own. And Allah knows best.

## Page 4257

Shaykh al-Islām, the mufti of mankind, unrivalled in his age and unique in his time, Taqī al-Dīn Abū al-Abbās Ahmad ibn Abd al-Halīm ibn Abd al-Salām Ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah have mercy on him and be pleased with him—was asked:

“If a man commits highway robbery and theft, or consumes what is unlawful, or does something similar, is this the provision that Allah Most High has guaranteed him, or not? Please give us a ruling; may you be rewarded.”

He answered:

Praise be to Allah. This is not the provision that Allah has made lawful for him. Allah neither loves nor approves of it, nor has He commanded him to spend from it. Such statements as His words, Most High:

“and spend out of what We have provided for them”

and His words, Most High:

“And spend from what We have provided for you”

do not include what is unlawful. Rather, Allah Most High condemns anyone who spends from unlawful wealth, and that person thereby deserves punishment in this world and the Hereafter, according to his religion.

Allah has said:

“And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly.”

This is consuming wealth unjustly.

Nevertheless, this is provision that Allah knew beforehand and decreed, as stated in the authentic hadith narrated by Ibn Masʿūd from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“The creation of each of you is gathered in his mother’s womb for forty days as a drop of fluid; then he becomes a clinging clot for a similar period; then he becomes a lump of flesh for a period like

---

## Page 4258

that; then Allah sends the angel to him, who is commanded to record four matters: his provision, his deeds, his lifespan, and whether he will be wretched or blessed.” Just as Allah has recorded the good and evil a person will do, while rewarding him for the good and punishing him for the evil, so too He has recorded the provision he will receive, whether lawful or unlawful, while punishing him for unlawful provision.

Thus, everything that exists comes about by Allah’s will and decree, as do all deeds. Yet divine decree excuses no one. Rather, it must be believed in, and no one may invoke it as an argument against Allah. Indeed, the conclusive argument belongs to Allah. Whoever invokes divine decree to justify committing sins has a groundless argument, and whoever offers it as an excuse has an unacceptable excuse. Such people resemble those who said:

“If Allah had willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have associated partners with Him.”

And those who said:

“If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them.”

As Allah Most High says:

“Lest a soul should say, ‘Alas for my neglect of my duty towards Allah! I was indeed among those who mocked.’”

“Or say, ‘If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.’”

As for the provision Allah has guaranteed His servants, He has guaranteed whoever fears Him that He will make a way out for him and provide for him from where he does not expect. As for someone who is not among those who fear Him, He has guaranteed him what befits him: He grants him the means to live in this world, then punishes him in the Hereafter. Thus He relates the words of His intimate friend:

“And provide its people with fruits—those among them who believe in Allah and the Last Day.”

Allah said:

“As for whoever disbelieves, I will grant him brief enjoyment, then compel him to the punishment of the Fire. What an evil destination!”

---

## Page 4259

And Allah has made provision lawful only for those who use it to help them obey Him, not for those who use it to help them disobey Him. Indeed, even though the latter consume the provision He has guaranteed them, He will punish them, as He says:

“As for whoever disbelieves, I will grant him brief enjoyment, then compel him to the punishment of the Fire. What an evil destination!”

Allah Most High also says:

“Livestock have been made lawful for you, except what is recited to you, but you are not permitted to hunt while in a state of consecration.”

Thus, He has permitted livestock only to those for whom hunting is forbidden during consecration. Allah Most High also says:

“There is no blame on those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have consumed, provided they fear Allah, believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good. And Allah loves those who do good.”

Thus, although every living being consumes the provision decreed for it, it is nevertheless punished for taking what has not been made lawful for it—whether because it is forbidden in itself or because it is used to aid disobedience to Allah. For this reason, the wealth of the disbelievers is not considered wrongfully seized; rather, it is lawful for the believers. It is called fayʾ (reverted wealth) when it returns to the believers, because wealth rightfully belongs only to those who obey Allah, not to those who use it to disobey Him. The believers therefore take it by virtue of their rightful entitlement, whereas the disbelievers transgress in spending it, just as they transgress in their deeds. When it returns to the believers, it has reverted to them, just as wealth reverts to its rightful owner.

## Page 4260

He was asked about wine and what is forbidden: “Is this Allah’s provision for the ignorant, or do they consume what has been decreed for them?”

He answered:

The word “provision” may mean what Allah Most High has made lawful for a person and granted him ownership of, or it may mean what a person feeds on.

The first sense is illustrated by His words:

“Spend from what We have provided you,”

and:

“And they spend out of what We have provided them.”

Provision in this sense is lawful and owned; it does not include wine or what is forbidden.

The second sense is illustrated by His words:

“There is no creature on earth whose provision is not assured by Allah.”

Allah Most High provides for animals, yet they are not described as owning property, nor as having received His permission in the religious sense, for animals bear no religious obligations—as is also the case with children and the mentally unsound. Nevertheless, this provision is neither their property nor forbidden to them.

Rather, what is forbidden is some of what a person feeds on. It forms part of the provision which Allah knew he would consume and decreed accordingly, as distinct from what He has made lawful and granted him ownership of. Thus, in the two Sahīh collections, Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The creation of each of you is brought together in his mother’s womb

---

## Page 4261

for forty days as a drop of fluid, then becomes a clinging clot for a similar period, then a lump of flesh for a similar period. Then the angel is sent and commanded to record four things. He is told: ‘Write down his provision, his lifespan, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or blessed.’ Then the spirit is breathed into him.

He said:

‘By Him in whose hand is my soul, one of you may perform the deeds of the people of Paradise until only a cubit separates him from it; then what has been written overtakes him, and he performs the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And one of you may perform the deeds of the people of the Fire until only a cubit separates him from it; then what has been written overtakes him, and he performs the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it.’”

Unlawful provision is among the things Allah has decreed and the angels have recorded. It falls within Allah’s will and creation. Nevertheless, He has forbidden it and prohibited it, so whoever partakes of it incurs such wrath, censure, and punishment from Him as he deserves. And Allah knows best.

## Page 4262

The shaykh—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked about the statement of Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir:

“I contended against the decrees of the True One by means of truth and for His sake.”

He replied:

All praise is due to Allah. Everything that happens occurs by Allah’s decree and predestination. Allah, glorified be He, has commanded us, as far as we are able, to remove evil through good, disbelief through faith, religious innovation through the Sunnah, and disobedience through obedience, both within ourselves and in our midst. Whoever commits disbelief, wickedness, or disobedience must repent, even though it occurred by Allah’s decree. He must also enjoin others to do what is right, forbid them from doing wrong as far as he is able, and strive in Allah’s cause.

Even though the wrong, disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience a person commits occur by Allah’s decree, he may not abandon striving for that through which Allah benefits him, relying instead on predestination. Rather, he must do what Allah and His Messenger have commanded. Muslim narrated in his Sahīh that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is good in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek Allah’s help, and do not give up. If something befalls you, do not say, ‘If only I had done such-and-such, this or that would have happened.’ Rather, say, ‘Allah decreed it, and He did what He willed,’ for ‘if only’ opens the way for Satan’s work.”

Thus, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded a person to strive for what benefits him; and what benefits him

---

## Page 4263

requires contending against the devils among humankind and jinn, and repelling decreed evil through the good that Allah has decreed. Alongside this, he must seek Allah’s help, for there is no power or strength except through Him, and his deeds must be sincerely devoted to Allah. Allah accepts only deeds done seeking His Face. This is the true meaning of your saying:

“You alone we worship,”

while the preceding requirement expresses the true meaning of:

“And You alone we ask for help.”

He must therefore worship Allah by doing what He has commanded and avoiding what He has forbidden, while seeking Allah’s help in doing so. Worshipping Allah and obeying His commands includes removing the evil He has decreed through the good He has decreed, and averting the evil Satan intends and strives to bring about before it arrives, through the good by which Allah repels it.

Allah Most High says:

“Were it not for Allah checking some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted.”

Thus, the evil that disbelievers and evildoers harbor within themselves and strive to bring about is repelled by rightful means, such as preparing military strength and keeping horses ready for battle, or through supplication and charity, both of which ward off affliction. As the hadith states:

“Supplication and affliction meet and wrestle between heaven and earth.”

Sometimes the cause of an evil has already taken shape and the evil is feared, so it is prevented from reaching its target—as when disbelievers are repelled if they advance upon Muslim lands. At other times, the evil has already occurred, so it is removed and evil deeds are replaced with good deeds. All of this comes under repelling decreed evil through decreed good. This is sometimes obligatory and sometimes recommended. What the shaykh—may Allah have mercy on him—mentioned is therefore what Allah and His Messenger have commanded.

## Page 4264

The point here is that many spiritual wayfarers and seekers contemplate the Lord’s lordship and the forbidden things He has decreed to occur. They go no further than contemplating this reality of His universal decree, supposing that this constitutes contentment with the divine decree and submission to it. This is ignorance and misguidance that may lead to disbelief and abandonment of the religion. Allah has not commanded us to be content with the disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience that occur. Rather, He has commanded us to hate them and repel them as far as we can. As the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“Whoever among you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand. If he cannot, then with his tongue. If he cannot, then with his heart—and that is the weakest level of faith.”

Allah Most High has said:

“He does not approve disbelief for His servants.”

And He has said:

“Allah does not love corruption.”

How, then, could He command us to be content for ourselves with what He does not approve for us? He has made the evil that occurs a trial and a test for us, as He Most High has said:

“We have made some of you a trial for others—will you be patient?”

After commanding fighting, He Most High said:

“Thus it is. Had Allah willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them, but He tests some of you by means of others. Those who are killed in Allah’s cause—He will never let their deeds go to waste.”

In Sahīh Muslim, it is reported that the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“By Him in whose hand is my soul, Allah decrees nothing for the believer except that it is good for him. This is true of no one but the believer: if prosperity comes his way, he is grateful, and that is good for him; if adversity befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him.”

Thus, when a believer is patient and grateful, the afflictions decreed for him are good

---

## Page 4265

for him. When he enjoins what is right, forbids what is wrong, and strives in Allah’s cause, the disbelief of the disbelievers that he is destined to encounter becomes a source of good for him. Likewise, when Satan and his own desires tempt him, that becomes a cause of the good he attains. Thus, if he resists and repels whatever evil is decreed, as Allah and His Messenger have commanded him, it becomes a means for him to attain righteousness and piety, goodness and reward, and higher ranks.
